home_pitcher_note: The reigning AL Cy Young Award winner will be making his fifth career Opening Day start. He is 14-3 with a 3.48 ERA in 23 career starts against the White Sox, including a 2-0 record and 2.57 ERA in three starts last year.
away_pitcher_note: After having his streak of five straight Opening Day starts snapped last season, Buehrle makes his sixth Game 1 start in the past seven years. He holds a 5-4 record at the newly dubbed Progressive Field.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona shocked the baseball world last year with a 19-8 season in which he had a 3.06 ERA in 32 starts. The only reason he was in the Tribe's rotation the first two months of the year was because Cliff Lee and Jake Westbrook suffered abdominal strains. Now, he's the club's bona fide No. 2 starter and a potential ace in the making.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez signed a three-year, $34.5 million extension prior to last season and then went out and pitched like a staff ace. Vazquez led all White Sox starters in wins, strikeouts and innings pitched (216 2/3). Vazquez's 213 strikeouts ranked as the sixth-best single-season total in franchise history and placed him fourth in the American League.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook turned his 2007 season around in the second half, particularly by going 4-1 with a 1.90 ERA in August. In 25 career starts against the Sox, Westbrook is 8-10 with a 5.06 ERA. He went 1-3 with a 5.70 ERA against them last year.
away_pitcher_note: It was a tale of two halves for the White Sox rookie in 2007. Before the All-Star break, Danks posted a 5-6 record with a manageable 4.62 ERA. Following the Midsummer Classic, Danks finished 1-7 with a 7.11 ERA and allowed 63 hits in 49 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Robertson has yet to lose his first outing of the season since breaking camp with the Tigers in 2004, including victories at home in his last two season debuts. That should give him some momentum going up against the White Sox, with whom he has had a rocky relationship in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Contreras ultimately could hold the key to his team's 2008 level of success. The big right-hander holds the franchise record with 17 straight winning decisions, a streak which ended in July 2006, but since the All-Star break, 2006, his 26 losses are the most in the Majors.

home_pitcher_note: Willis will make his American League debut under the spotlight of a home crowd and a FOX network regional broadcast, starting what he hopes is a rebound campaign following season highs in losses and ERA in his final season for Florida last year. He pitched through command issues in Spring Training, but the mid-90s velocity on his fastball gives the Tigers reason for encouragement.
His last time out, Verlander allowed four earned runs on four hits in six innings in his first Opening Day start. He gave up just one hit through five, but struggled with location in his last inning.
away_pitcher_note: It was an uncharacteristically short and disastrous start for the left-hander on Monday in Cleveland, as he made his sixth Opening Day start in seven years. Buehrle cruised through the first inning unscathed, only to allow seven runs on seven hits before he could record the third out of the second. Buehrle did throw 30 of his 48 pitches for strikes, but according to catcher A.J. Pierzynski, threw the ball too hard and lost some of his movement. Buehrle has five days before his next start, wrapping up this six-game road trip to start the season Sunday night in Detroit. Buehrle has a lifetime 12-8 record against Detroit and a 6-5 record at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander struggled with his control during Wednesday's 2008 debut, throwing 103 pitches over just five innings. Vazquez struck out six but also walked four, including Ryan Garko and Franklin Gutierrez consecutively with two outs in the fifth inning to force home a run. A two-out walk given to Kelly Shoppach in the second set up Grady Sizemore's two-run single. Vazquez gets the call for the White Sox home opener against Minnesota, coming off an 8-5 showing with a 3.57 ERA over 16 starts at U.S. Cellular Field in 2007. Vazquez has a 4-5 career mark against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn was impressive in his first Major League start, holding the Angels to just one run on five hits over seven innings. The right-hander didn't appear to be intimidated against a potent Angels lineup, attacking hitters like Vladimir Guerrero, who struck out twice in his three at-bats facing Blackburn. Next up for Blackburn will be a test on the road, as he'll pitch for the first time at U.S. Cellular Field against the White Sox. Last season, he threw two scoreless innings of relief against Chicago in the Metrodome.

home_pitcher_note: If Thursday's first start serves as any indication, the second-year southpaw appears primed for a big season in 2008. Danks held the Indians hitless for five innings, before allowing Casey Blake's single to center to start the sixth. Danks exited after 6 2/3 innings, giving up one earned run, while striking out two and walking two. Danks also recorded 11 outs via the ground ball. He has a 1-2 record with a 5.63 ERA against Minnesota, and a 3-6 career mark at home.
away_pitcher_note: Baker didn't show any signs of the setbacks he endured in Spring Training during his first start of the season. Baker limited the Royals to just three runs on seven hits over 6 2/3 innings. More importantly he was able to throw 84 pitches without any problems. Baker's health is key for a rotation that's already endured its first setback with Kevin Slowey's strained right biceps muscle. Baker will remain on regular five-day rest and face the White Sox on Wednesday at U.S. Cellular Field in his next start. Baker is 1-2 with a 9.14 ERA in five career starts against Chicago.

home_pitcher_note: Although the White Sox did not lose the game, it was not exactly the start to the 2008 season sought out by Contreras. It was especially true after Contreras'  dismal 2007 showing. The right-hander had trouble finding the strike zone, walking four in five-plus innings and throwing just 56 of his 92 pitches for strikes. Contreras yielded four earned runs on 10 hits, striking out two, but also losing his rhythm early on in the game. He faces the Tigers once again, this time on six days rest following Thursday's rainout.
away_pitcher_note: Willis put up an interesting line in his first start for his new team. He allowed three earned runs on just one hit and had a no-hitter through five innings, But he issued seven walks, retaining his control problems from Spring Training. He will make his second career start at U.S. Cellular Field. He left in the second inning with arm troubles in his only other start there.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander became the first White Sox starter to pick up a victory during the team's initial run through the starting five, allowing three runs on three hits over six innings. Floyd was touched up by Brandon Inge's two-run home run in the fourth, but he only walked two and gave up five other hits. He exited after just 87 pitches, raising his record to 2-0 over his past three appearances at Comerica Park, with an extra day off in between starts. Floyd gets the call again against the Tigers, with this effort coming in Chicago, where Floyd has a career mark of 0-3 with a 6.55 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander allowed a career-high nine nuns in his last start, a 13-2 loss to the White Sox on Sunday night, although four of the runs were unearned. He was sharp at times, but struggled with his command in his last two innings. He also allowed a home run to Nick Swisher on his second pitch of the game.

home_pitcher_note: Much like Mark Buehrle, Vazquez bounced back nicely in his second start of 2008 after a rough debut performance in Cleveland. The right-hander struck out eight and walked just one over seven innings, allowing three runs on seven hits. He had a defeat turned into victory courtesy of Joe Crede's seventh-inning grand slam. Vazquez faces his third different American League Central opponent in three starts, carrying a 4-4 record with a 4.73 ERA lifetime against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers battled his command much more in his second outing of the season after a quality start in his first, but he gave his struggling team a chance at a victory in both circumstances. Nevertheless, he's 0-2 after two starts in a season for the first time since 1995. He struggled in two starts on Chicago's south side last season after allowing just two earned runs over 20 innings there in 2006, but the difference was partly due to the difference in his health.

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle gained a form of redemption Sunday night, after getting pummeled for seven runs on seven hits over 1 2/3 innings during his Opening Day start in Cleveland on Monday. Against the Tigers, Buehrle yielded two runs on seven hits over seven innings, walking two and striking out one. Buehrle induced double-play grounders in the fourth, fifth, sixth and seventh innings in order to stem the Tigers� damage. Due to Tuesday�s off-day and Thursday�s rainout, Buehrle will have seven days in between starts. He was pushed back to face Oakland because of their left-handed laden lineup. Buehrle has a 3-9 record with a 3.86 ERA lifetime against the A�s, but most of that trouble has come in Oakland, where he is 0-6.
away_pitcher_note: Smith made his much-anticipated Major League debut in his last outing against the Blue Jays. The 24-year-old lefty, who was acquired as part of an offseason trade that sent No.1 starter Dan Haren to the Diamondbacks, survived a rough first inning en route to allowing three runs on two hits while striking out five. Smith did struggle with his control, though, surrendering five walks over six innings of work. A spot in Oakland's starting rotation was created for Smith when right-hander Justin Duchscherer was placed on the 15-day disabled list with a strained right biceps.

home_pitcher_note: The strong showing made by the southpaw during his first start of the year in Cleveland was balanced out by the shellacking administered by the Twins during Wednesday?s loss at U.S. Cellular Field. Danks allowed seven runs on seven hits over 2 1/3 innings, struggling with his control from the outset. He walked three and struck out two, exiting after walking Craig Monroe with the bases loaded in the third. Danks won his only previous career start against Oakland, allowing one run over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Eveland continued to impress the Oakland brain trust with an impressive outing in his last start against the Blue Jays. Making just his second start with the Athletics, Eveland tossed 6 1/3 shutout innings. The 24-year-old surrendered just three hits while striking out six batters and threw 53 of his 95 pitches for strikes. Eveland credited the majority of his success against Toronto to establishing his fastball and curveball combination early in the game before mixing in a slider and changeup to keep the Jays hitters off-balance.

home_pitcher_note: Loewen has been shaky in both of his starts this season, but he'll get an extra day of rest before his next outing. The southpaw worked five erratic innings in the second game of last Thursday's doubleheader, but he escaped with a no-decision. Loewen experienced shoulder fatigue in Spring Training, but has said that it isn't a concern.
away_pitcher_note: It was a step in the right direction for Contreras, who really fell victim to one poor inning during a 5-2 loss to Detroit. Contreras allowed four runs on six hits over 6 2/3 innings, but three of those runs and four of those hits came in the third inning. Contreras walked three and struck out two, throwing 60 of his 102 pitches for strikes. The right-hander opens the White Sox five-game road trip in Baltimore, carrying a 3-4 career record with a 5.50 ERA against the Orioles. Contreras is 1-1 with a 7.00 ERA at Camden Yards.

home_pitcher_note: Guthrie has worked into the seventh inning of each of his last two starts, and he's had a late rally erase him as the pitcher of record in both of them. Guthrie trailed Seattle two starts ago, but was the beneficiary of a ninth-inning rally, and he owned a lead in last Friday's start against Tampa Bay before the bullpen gave it away late.
away_pitcher_note: For 7 1/3 innings on Saturday against Detroit, Floyd flirted with history. His quest to throw the 17th no-hitter in White Sox franchise history came to an end on Edgar Renteria's sharp single to right-center, which also brought an end to Floyd's afternoon after 107 pitches. Floyd struck out four and walked four in what could be a coming-of-age start for the 25-year-old, once again extending his mastery over Detroit, and improving to 3-0 in his last five starts against the Tigers. Floyd moves away from Detroit and into Camden Yards, where he has never pitched.

home_pitcher_note: The 25-year old is coming off an impressive Major League debut on Sunday, in which he held Baltimore to just one run over six innings. The righty scattered six hits, and he allowed only one walk while striking out five. At 6-foot-9, Niemann is an intimidating pitcher, and when he is in command, his sinking fastball is extremely hard for opposing batters to dig out.
away_pitcher_note: Make it two straight stellar starts for Vazquez, who allowed only one Detroit runner to reach second base during Sunday's 11-0 victory over the Tigers at U.S. Cellular Field. Vazquez did not issue a walk, while striking out nine over seven innings. He gave up a Gary Sheffield double and four singles among his 92 pitches, of which 69 were thrown for strikes. Vazquez moves out of the American League Central, having faced Cleveland, Minnesota and Detroit to open the season, and he will begin the weekend set against the Rays. Vazquez has a 4-2 career record against Tampa Bay, with a 4.66 ERA.
summary: 2008-04-18 - Chicago White Sox (9) @ Tampa Bay Rays (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Sonnanstine is coming off a rocky outing on April 14 in which he was charged with nine hits and seven runs over 3 1/3 innings. The Rays went on to lose to the Yankees, 8-7. A usually reliable pitcher, Sonnanstine will look to bounce back after equaling career highs for runs (seven) and home runs (three) allowed in a game.
away_pitcher_note: Buehrle pitched OK in his previous start, allowing two runs and nine hits over seven innings against Oakland, but he was beaten by rookie lefty Greg Smith. Buehrle?s dense ERA comes mostly from a blowup against the Indians in his first start. He is 6-1 with a 4.13 ERA in his career against Tampa, including 5-1 at Tropicana Field. The loss came in 2002.
summary: 2008-04-19 - Chicago White Sox (0) @ Tampa Bay Rays (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander has struggled with consistency throughout his career and has been no different in 2008. Jackson started the year 2-0, pitching a two-hit shutout over eight innings on April 10, but followed it up with a mediocre performance vs. New York. The powerful hurler had four strikeouts, but also allowed four walks and five hits, and was tagged for five runs in five innings. He will look to bounce back against Chicago, a team he has only faced once before, earning a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Celebrating his 23rd birthday, the talented southpaw held the A's scoreless for 7 2/3 innings during a 4-1 victory on Tuesday. Danks gave up five hits, walked two and struck out four, as he ended an 11-start winless drought and won for the first time since July 16, 2007. He has a 1-0 record with a 7.20 ERA lifetime against the Rays, picking up that one victory in his only start at Tropicana Field. Danks and Buehrle will work back-to-back for the last time, with a switch most likely coming after Monday's off-day.
summary: 2008-04-20 - Chicago White Sox (6) @ Tampa Bay Rays (0) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Contreras picked up his first victory in '08 with a show of resounding dominance on the mound and not much offensive support behind him. The big right-hander made Jim Thome's three-run home run in the first inning stand up over seven, as he allowed one run, before giving way to Scott Linebrink and Bobby Jenks after 91 pitches. Contreras struck out six and yielded four hits, but most importantly, he did not issue a single walk. Contreras, who pitched for the Yankees during the 2003 and 2004 seasons, has a 2-4 record against his original big-league employer.
away_pitcher_note: It wasn't pretty for Wang on Wednesday at Yankee Stadium, where he was unable to make it through the fifth inning during a home game for the first time in his big league career. Facing the Red Sox for the second time this season, Wang couldn't command the strike zone and tied a career high with eight runs allowed in a no-decision. He allowed a two-run homer to Kelly Shoppach and was removed after walking the first two batters in the sixth inning. He remained winless for the season and the Dodgers have scored eight runs while he was in the game during his six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Danks' debut performance in the Crosstown Showdown was one to remember, holding the Cubs to one run on five hits over six innings in a no-decision. The left-hander struck out five, but more importantly, didn't issue a walk in throwing 56 of his 85 pitches for strikes. From the last out in the second to Kosuke Fukudome's one-out single in the sixth, Danks retired 11 straight. The southpaw, who has never faced the Dodgers, has allowed two earned runs or less this year in 12 of his 15 starts. Danks also has worked seven innings or more in just two of his trips to the mound but has gone at last six innings on 10 occasions.
summary: 2008-06-26 - Chicago White Sox (2) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (0) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Contreras got lit up by the Cubs in the fourth inning Sunday. After allowing just one Cubs run to that point, Contreras got touched up for eight more via three home runs, four singles and a walk. It was Contreras' third-straight loss and by far the worst start of the season for the right-hander. His ERA has risen more than a point since his last win, which came on June 5 against Kansas City. In five career starts against the Cubs, Contreras is 1-3 with a 6.39 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster nearly notched his second complete game in three starts in his last outing. He went eight-plus innings against the White Sox, giving up one run on 10 hits for the win. The right-hander improved to 9-0 at home, and pitching on the South Side will be as close to home as he can get. Dempster has 10 quality starts this season, and is making the transition from closer to starter look very smooth. His game plan? Attack the hitters, and let his defense do the work.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez has struggled in his last four outings, allowing at least four earned runs in each start. He walked five on Sunday against the Cubs and gave up five runs, though only four were earned. His ERA, which was just 3.43 on May 21, has gone up nearly a point in the last month. He's walked 16 batters in the six starts since then and struck out just 29 -- a subpar ratio for the flamethrower. Vazquez is 3-4 lifetime against the Cubs with an ERA just under 5.00.
away_pitcher_note: Gallagher still needs to trust his second and third pitches. He did not get a decision in his last start, against Tampa Bay, giving up one run, unearned, on four hits over six innings. It was a good outing because he escaped some tough jams. But his side sessions are key as the young right-hander works on his breaking pitches to compliment his fastball.

home_pitcher_note: It was a momentous night for Buehrle, as the White Sox ace left-hander struck out two during a 6-1 victory over the Dodgers, which gave him exactly 1,000 strikeouts for his career. Buehrle pitched exactly eight innings for his fourth straight start, allowing one run on six hits, and not issuing a walk. Buehrle now has a 3-0 record with a 1.36 ERA over his last four starts, allowing five earned runs in 32 innings. Buehrle has a 3-4 record with a 5.10 ERA lifetime against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Marshall gets his second and likely last start in place of the injured Carlos Zambrano. He flashed strong pitching, with seven strikeouts, but was eventually chased by the Orioles after giving up four runs in 4 2/3 innings on Tuesday. The loss ended the Cubs' 14-game home winning streak. Marshall is 1-1 with a 2.92 ERA career against the White Sox and tossed 6 1/3 innings of shutout ball against the crosstown rivals in 2007.

home_pitcher_note: The Dodgers jumped on the White Sox right-hander for two runs on three hits in the first inning of Wednesday's 5-0 loss, and Floyd never seemed to recover. He allowed four earned runs on six hits over 5 1/3 innings, striking out two and walking two. Floyd also has some trouble pitching around mistakes behind him, giving up his 13th unearned run against the Dodgers, tops in the Majors. Floyd has a 1-0 record with a 6.00 ERA against the Indians this season and is 1-1 with a 4.38 ERA lifetime against Cleveland.
away_pitcher_note: Although he picked up the loss, Sowers gave the Tribe a quality start in his last outing, going seven innings in Wednesday's effort against the Giants. Yes, his control was a bit erratic at times (five walks), he seemingly couldn't keep the ball in the infield (nine hits) and he found trouble early (two first-inning runs), but the left-hander showed better command of his fastball, which allowed him to mitigate the damage (three runs). Up and down from Triple-A Buffalo all season, Sowers has yet to face the White Sox in 2008. He faced them last year, though, giving up two runs in six innings for a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Danks closed out the month of June with another quality start, hurling six scoreless innings against the Dodgers during Thursday afternoon's series finale. Danks now has thrown 11 straight scoreless innings and ranks third in the American League for lowest ERA. He struck out three and walked four against the Dodgers, throwing 106 pitches overall, and worked out of two jams with a runner on third and less than two outs. Danks has no record in one start against Cleveland this season and has a 1-2 mark with a 4.44 ERA lifetime against the Indians. Danks also picked up his first career Interleague victory and first big league hit on Thursday.
away_pitcher_note: Lee continued his campaign to be the American League's starting pitcher for the All-Star Game with another impressive start Thursday against the Giants. And this time he was actually awarded for it. The left-hander went eight innings, striking out a career-high 11 and, thanks mostly to his precisely located fastball, never really had to escape trouble to pick up his 11th win of the season. He continues to be bright spot for the Indians in 2008, especially after a rough 2007, where he was sent to Triple-A Buffalo to work out of a season-long funk. Lee has yet to face the White Sox this season, but he has faced them the most out of any opponent for his career. In 17 appearances -- 15 starts -- Lee is 4-5 with a 6.61 ERA against the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Contreras gave up three runs in six-plus innings in his second start against the Cubs on Friday. The performance was good enough for the right-hander to pick up his seventh win, though manager Ozzie Guillen knew how much his pitcher struggled throughout the start. The win snapped a three-game losing streak during which he'd allowed 18 runs in 16 innings. His ERA has gone from a season-low 2.76 before the losing streak to just under four. Contreras has faced Cleveland once this year, giving up just one run over six innings at U.S. Cellular Field on May 20.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia continued his hot streak since late April with another strong start. His latest victim, the Reds on Friday, managed just four hits while striking out 11 times over eight innings. The big left-hander was nearly unhittable after the second inning, retiring 15 batters in a row at one point. He's had mixed results against the White Sox this season, though, allowing five runs in 5 1/3 innings of work in an Opening Day no-decision. He pitched much better the second time around, but this time picked up the loss after a seven-inning, two-run effort. Lifetime against the White Sox, Sabathia has been much better, as he carries a 14-4 record and 3.61 ERA in 25 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez simply hasn't pitched well for the White Sox recently, and manager Ozzie Guillen said after his latest start that the staff ace needs to start challenging hitters more. Vazquez lasted just 4 1/3 innings against the Cubs on Saturday, his shortest outing of the season. He allowed five runs for a fourth consecutive start, despite striking out seven batters. He owns a 7.48 ERA in his last five outings. Vazquez hasn't faced the Athletics this season, but has seen them five times in his career with little success. He's 1-2 with a 6.60 ERA lifetime against them.
away_pitcher_note: Despite getting the loss in a close 1-0 game in his last start against the Giants, Duchscherer made yet another case for his second career All-Star appearance. He didn't allow a hit until the fourth inning, when he gave up two before going the next four innings without surrendering another one. In his eight innings of work, he walked just one and struck out four while throwing 97 pitches. In 13 relief appearances against Chicago, Duchscherer is 3-1 with a 2.76 ERA. He has given up five runs on 13 hits in 16 1/3 innings versus the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle is looking more and more like the White Sox ace of old with each passing start. To illustrate that point, the seven innings he pitched Sunday were the fewest in his last five starts. He surrendered just one unearned run to the Cubs and picked up his third-straight victory. Buehrle is 4-0 in his last five starts with an accompanying 1.15 ERA.  He's faced Oakland once this year and pitched far too well to have earned the loss. He allowed two earned runs in seven innings and exited the game trailing 2-1.
away_pitcher_note: After throwing three innings of no-hit ball in his last start, Blanton gave up a string of five consecutive hits in the fourth against the Giants en route to surrendering seven runs on eight hits while pitching into the fifth inning -- the second time in his last three starts he's given up seven runs or more. Blanton will look to get back on track against the White Sox, against whom he owns a 2-1 record with a 3.12 ERA in three career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Floyd looked much better Monday against the Indians than he had in either of his previous two starts. He allowed four runs -- three earned -- and struck out a career-high 10 batters. The only player that got the better of him was Jhonny Peralta, who smacked three of the seven hits he allowed. Two of the hits were doubles and the other was a home run. Floyd attributed the quality start to the return of his offspeed command. He hadn't been able to throw his changeup for strikes in his previous starts. Floyd has never faced the Athletics.
away_pitcher_note: Oakland's lone rookie in the starting rotation, Smith was outstanding his last time out, beating the Angels by holding them to one run -- a solo home run -- on four hits while walking two and striking out three in the first complete game of his career Monday in Anaheim. Owner of one of the best pickoff moves in the game, Smith has nailed an MLB-high eight runners and now controls the opponents' running game on reputation alone. He's pitched more than seven innings only once, on April 29, in part because the A's are being cautious as he closes in on his 2007 Minor League innings total of 122. Smith, who picked up his first big league win by holding the White Sox to six hits over seven innings on April 14, has made 16 starts and has thrown 99 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Danks threw one of his best outings of the season and one of the best of his career Tuesday night against the Indians. His eight innings and eight strikeouts tied career highs, and he allowed just one earned run on four hits and a walk. He didn't factor in the decision, though. Danks has allowed only eight earned runs in his last six starts and has just one win to show for it. He's faced Oakland once this season and surrendered no runs over 7 2/3 innings. It was arguably his best start of the season before the gem he threw Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Harden, who had dominated the Phillies with eight innings of two-hit work his previous time out, wasn't nearly as strong Tuesday in Anaheim, where he threw 91 pitches while allowing two runs on five hits and a walk while striking out five over five innings before leaving with the game tied. Harden, who didn't throw any breaking balls against the Phillies, relied heavily on his changeup against the Angels but occasionally popped 94 mph on the stadium radar gun. Since the start of the 2005 season, Harden is 1-1 with a 3.71 ERA in three starts against the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: After breezing through three innings on Thursday at Baltimore, Davies ran into a wall. He was pummeled for seven runs on seven hits -- including Aubrey Huff's two homers -- in the next inning-plus. The Royals rallied to take him off the hook but this was the third straight start in which Davies was roughed up. Before that, he'd  had four superb outings since being recalled from Triple-A. Davies has pitched just once against the White Sox, losing, 6-1, last Aug. 19 when he lasted just 4 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Contreras hasn't looked anything like the pitcher he was in April and May. His season-low 2.76 ERA on June 5 has swelled above four over his last five starts. He managed a quality start against the Indians on Wednesday, but the outcome was better than the performance would indicate. He surrendered four runs, three of which were earned, over six innings. He allowed six hits and tied a season high by issuing four free passes. He loaded the bases twice but got out of each inning with minimal damage. He did not factor in the decision and is 1-3 in his last five starts. He has faced Kansas City once this season, allowing one run in seven innings
summary: 2008-07-08 - Chicago White Sox (8) @ Kansas City Royals (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Bannister got knocked around in Friday night's start against the red-hot Rays. The right-hander allowed seven runs (six earned) on eight hits and made an early exit after five innings. He has struggled in road appearances this season, posting a 2-5 record and an 8.36 ERA away from Kauffman Stadium. Although Bannister has been erratic on the mound, his control was not a problem in Friday's loss, as he issued only one walk. With losses in his last two starts, Bannister will look to bounce back against the White Sox. He is 2-1 in five starts vs. Chicago, with a 6.65 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Although it ended in defeat, Vazquez produced his best start since May 31 during Thursday's 3-2 loss to Oakland. Vazquez had allowed five runs in each of his last four starts, but gave up just three runs on four hits during the 23rd complete game of his career. Vazquez fanned 10, including seven over the first three innings, giving him 35 career games with double-digit strikeouts. Vazquez threw a season-high 123 pitches, after making a change in mechanics to keep his hands closer to the body during his windup. He has not faced the Royals in 2008 but has a 6-2 career record with a 2.74 ERA against Kansas City and a 2-0 mark at Kauffman Stadium.
summary: 2008-07-09 - Chicago White Sox (7) @ Kansas City Royals (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Greinke got the loss on Saturday night, but the young right-hander certainly pitched well enough to win. A two-out double to Akinori Iwamura scored both of Greinke's charged runs, and he went on to fan seven Rays in the seven-inning losing effort. He tossed 70 of 113 pitches for strikes and will look to get some support from the Royals offense in the home contest vs. the White Sox.
away_pitcher_note: Buehrle's month of July didn't exactly start like his most impressive month of June, during which he won four straight and posted a 1.60 ERA over six consecutive quality starts. Oakland touched up Buehrle for four runs on 10 hits over 5 2/3 innings Friday. Buehrle threw 105 pitches, struck out five and walked three, as he slipped to 3-11 lifetime against the A's. Buehrle features a 16-6 career mark when facing the Royals, along with a 3.40 ERA, and has an 8-4 ledger at Kauffman Stadium.
summary: 2008-07-10 - Chicago White Sox (1) @ Kansas City Royals (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Mendoza never got comfortable in Monday's 9-6 Rangers loss to the Angels, allowing eight runs in 1 1/3 innings. The rookie right-hander said he felt great in the bullpen, but when he got on the mound, his mechanics and location were off. He allowed three home runs and nine hits. Mendoza is 0-3 with a 6.60 ERA in five starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Entering the 2008 season, Floyd had a rather inauspicious 8-10 career record with a disastrous 6.30 ERA. Following Saturday's dominant effort against Oakland, Floyd improved to 10-4 and watched his ERA drop to 3.22 in 2008 alone. Yes, it has been a coming-of-age effort for the right-hander. Floyd pitched scoreless baseball for 7 1/3 innings against Oakland, giving up three hits and three walks, while fanning six. Floyd has one career no-decision against the Rangers, working six innings and allowing three runs on six hits, while striking out four and walking two. This start came at the Rangers' home ballpark, as will his final first-half trip to the mound.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood wasn't at his best in Baltimore his last time out, but he was good enough to earn his second road victory of the season. In five innings he allowed five runs, three earned, on nine hits and struck out two. However, the offense and bullpen kept him in line for the victory. Millwood is now 4-1 in eight starts since coming off the disabled list. Millwood will face the White Sox for the first time this season. He's 1-2 against Chicago in seven career starts despite having a 2.15 ERA, 1.09 WHIP and .229 batting average against in 46 innings.
away_pitcher_note: If not for pitching through an amazing eight no-decisions in 18 starts this season, Danks probably would have been a 2008 All-Star. Danks was impressive once again during Sunday's effort against Oakland, allowing two runs on four hits over 6 1/3 innings. The left-hander no-hit the A's through five innings and struck out a career-high nine in the victory. The Texas native and one-time top pick of the Rangers has faced his former team on just one prior occasion. Danks suffered a loss last year in Texas, allowing five runs on seven hits over 5 2/3 innings, with just two of those runs being earned.

home_pitcher_note: Harrison's numbers weren't astounding in his Major League debut, but he gave the Rangers just what they needed. Called up from Triple-A Oklahoma to start in place of Eric Hurley, who was placed on the DL with a strained left hamstring, Harrison went seven innings and allowed just two runs on five hits and a walk while striking out one. He faced the minimum in five different innings. It was the longest outing for a Rangers pitcher in his Major League debut since August, 2000. Harrison will try to put together another solid start in his first meeting with the White Sox Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: A no-decision was no doubt fine with Contreras in his last outing, which came on Tuesday against Kansas City. He gave up five runs in six-plus innings and never seemed in control. By the third inning, he had thrown nearly 70 pitches. In two July starts, he has two no-decisions. It's been better than his June, when he went 2-3 with a 6.83 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle will come out of the break looking to end a personal two-game losing streak. In his last two starts he's allowed six runs, four earned, on 16 hits and three walks while he's struck out 13 in as many innings. However, he's received a grand total of two runs of support in those two starts. His last loss was especially hard to take. Buehrle had a 1-0 lead going into the eighth, but two unearned runs scored that inning off him, reversing the decision. Buehrle will face Kansas City, a club he's logged his second most career innings against, a second straight time. He's 16-7 all-time against the Royals with a 3.29 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke pitched quite well again in his last outing on July 10 against the White Sox in Kansas City but didn't get the victory. He gave up one run in seven innings -- on Jermaine Dye's monster home run -- but the Royals didn't come back to win until after he'd left the game. He'd also pitched well in his previous start at Tampa Bay but lost, 3-0. And three times this year Greinke got no decision after leaving the game with a lead. The bottom line is he deserves to have a higher win total. This will be his third go against the White Sox this year; they hammered him once, he stopped them once.
summary: 2008-07-18 - Kansas City Royals (5) @ Chicago White Sox (9) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Floyd lasted just 2 2/3 innings his last time out at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington. He never really had control of any of his pitches against Texas as he walked a career-high seven batters and gave up a season-high six earned runs. Floyd has had a trend of alternating decisions this season, which would put him in line for a victory against Kansas City Saturday. He won his only start against the Royals this season, allowing four runs, two earned, in seven innings while striking out four.
away_pitcher_note: Meche's last outing was July 12 against the Mariners and he zipped through five scoreless innings before being hit by a four-spot in the sixth. He was tagged for 10 hits, the most he's given up this season, in 6 2/3 innings but he walked just one. Meche had no decision, as the Royals came back to win. He was successful in improving his control, making 98 pitches after using up 115 in the 5 1/3 innings of his previous start.
summary: 2008-07-19 - Kansas City Royals (9) @ Chicago White Sox (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The native Texan won in his second career start in his home state and gave himself consecutive victories for the first time since winning on April 15 and 20 this season. Danks faced the minimum in five innings against the Rangers and had held them to just two runs until they scored twice more on him in the eighth inning. The bullpen held onto his lead, though, to give him his seventh win of the season. He struck out eight in the outing, giving him three straight starts with at least that many strikeouts. Danks will next face the Royals, who he received a no-decision against earlier in the season. He's yet to figure in a decision in two career starts against Kansas City.
away_pitcher_note: In his last pre-break outing, Bannister limited the White Sox to four hits but those included a pair of two-run homers by Carlos Quentin and a single run on a walk and a double. Bannister lasted 6 2/3 innings, giving up five runs in all, and had no decision. Except for the two fastballs that Quentin belted out of the park, Bannister thought he pitched pretty well. But in his last three starts, he's surrendered seven, six and five earned runs -- 18 in 16 1/3 innings. Against the Sox in his career, he's 2-1 with a 6.67 ERA.
summary: 2008-07-20 - Kansas City Royals (8) @ Chicago White Sox (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez will endure the longest layoff between starts of Chicago's starters, going 12 days since his start on July 9 at Kansas City. That outing, Vazquez was tagged for six runs on 11 hits in 5 2/3 innings, but he avoided taking a loss. In addition to the nearly two weeks between starts for Vazquez, he hasn't earned a victory in over a month -- June 17 against Pittsburgh. He's allowed at least four runs in all but one start since June 6. He'll be thrown right back into the fire for his first start of the season against Texas' high-powered offense. Vazquez is 2-1 in four career starts against the Rangers, despite posting a 6.29 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Eric Hurley was scratched with a sore arm, so the Rangers tabbed Feldman to take his place. After compiling mostly solid numbers in May and June, Feldman had a rough start to July. He was scheduled to return as a member of the bullpen, but instead will step right into the starting rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle made one mistake in his start on Friday night against the Royals. His 1-0 offering to Billy Butler in the sixth inning traveled 431 feet over the left-field wall for a three-run homer. Fortunately for Buehrle, the White Sox still had a three-run lead. The left-hander allowed just four hits and four runs, three of which were earned, in seven innings of work. It was his first win in his past three starts, and one that moved him past Joel Horlen into seventh place on the White Sox all-time victories list. Buehrle has not faced the Rangers this season, but is 9-3 with a 2.97 ERA lifetime against them. He will be working on three days' rest, moving up one day because he will return to Missouri on Wednesday for his grandfather's funeral. The White Sox did not want Buehrle to miss his turn in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Mendoza will come right back and face the Chicago White Sox after allowing only a run in six innings in a 7-2 victory over the Sox on July 11. The Rangers want to see more of the pitcher that challenged hitters in that game. Mendoza had eight strikeouts after not recording any in his previous start against the Angels, a game in which he allowed eight runs in 1 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander, who once played quarterback for the University of Michigan, makes his Major League debut during Wednesday afternoon's series finale. Richard will be taking the spot of Jose Contreras, placed on the disabled list with right elbow tendinitis. Richard posted a 12-6 record with a 2.44 ERA between stops this season at Double-A Birmingham and Triple-A Charlotte. He won all six of his starts for the Knights, striking out 29 and walking just four over 38 innings, while producing a 2.47 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood continued his career-long difficulty against Minnesota on Friday, going 6 1/3 innings while allowing five earned runs on 11 hits in the 6-0 Rangers loss. Millwood is now 0-6 career against the Twins. Millwood will next take on the White Sox. He allowed 10 hits and five earned runs in 5 1/3 innings against Chicago on July 12, a 9-7 Rangers loss.

home_pitcher_note: Robertson took the mound last Saturday at Baltimore with a six-run lead, but it was gone by the end of the third. So was Robertson, whom the Orioles hit around for seven runs on eight hits -- six of them singles -- over 2 1/3 innings. He has battled high hit totals in four of his last five starts, the exception being nine innings of one-run ball July 6 at Seattle. He's keeping the ball on the ground, but they aren't resulting in the outs that he needs. Robertson has split his two starts against the White Sox this season, including 6 1/3 innings of three-run ball to beat them on June 10 in Detroit.
away_pitcher_note: Despite a quality start against the Royals, Floyd picked up his second loss in a row Saturday night at U.S. Cellular Field. He gave up three runs in the sixth, but only one was earned. Ross Gload hit a hard grounder toward Joe Crede that bounced off his glove and continued rolling into left field. The error led to John Buck's home run the next at-bat and the White Sox never recovered. Floyd walked three more batters in the game, too, having now issued at least three free passes in each of his past three starts. Floyd faced Detroit in back-to-back starts to open the season. He gave up a combined three runs in 13 1/3 innings to pick up his first two wins.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander has ascended from the depths of a 2-9 record in early June to now sit within a victory of .500. Not only has he gone 6-0 with a 2.30 ERA over his past eight starts, but he has given up two runs or fewer in each of those outings. He fell an out shy of a complete game last Sunday at Baltimore, allowing a run on three hits while throwing 105 pitches in sweltering heat. He's 1-2 against the White Sox this season and 2-6 against them in his career, but he started this run of his with a complete-game four-hitter against Chicago on June 11.
away_pitcher_note: Danks was uncharacteristically off his game Sunday against the Royals. The left-hander lasted just four innings, surrendering four runs on nine hits and two walks. It was the first time he gave up more then four runs since allowing seven on April 9 against Minnesota. His offense bailed him out of the loss. He hasn't been handed a loss since May 24. He'll try to get back on track against Detroit, perhaps helped by the fact that the Tigers have yet to see Danks this year. He was 0-1 with a 5.71 ERA in three starts against them last year.

home_pitcher_note: As Jim Leyland said, Miner was just what the doctor ordered. The Tigers needed a No. 5 starter, and Miner filled in the role perfectly Monday. In his first start since early 2007, he pitched six scoreless innings. Miner's control had improved greatly since his last relief outing, as he mixed mainly fastballs and changeups. Leyland wants Miner to improve his breaking ball if he wants to stick in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez literally made one mistake over seven innings during Monday's contest against the Rangers, but that mistake ended up costing him a chance at victory. Vazquez's 2-0 offering to Josh Hamilton with two outs in the third was deposited over the center field fence for a three-run home run, giving Texas all the runs it would need in a 6-1 victory. Vazquez fanned 10, producing his 36th career double-digit strikeout effort, and he also allowed four hits and walked two. Vazquez has lost three straight decisions and has not won since June 17. He has a 1-1 record with a 3.46 ERA against Detroit this season, with a 0-1 record at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Some late struggles by the right-hander turned a good start against the Yankees into a less than pleasing one. Slowey gave up three runs in his final one-third of an inning, including a two-run homer to Bobby Abreu. The homer by the Yankees right fielder was the 13th long ball that Slowey has given up in 15 starts this season. Keeping the ball inside the park has been a challenge for the pitcher and one he'll have to do better with as he faces the White Sox for the third time this season. He is 0-2 against Chicago in two starts in ’08, having allowed 11 earned runs over just eight innings.
away_pitcher_note: Pitching on just three days' rest for the fourth time in his career, Buehrle was as dominant as he has been since the start of June. The southpaw allowed one run on six hits over 7 1/3 innings, striking out three and not issuing a walk in winning his second straight decision. He improved to 6-2 over his last nine starts and 7-3 in his last 13, picking up his 10th career victory against Texas. Buehrle has a 1-1 record with a 5.27 ERA in two starts this season against the Twins but has not yet pitched at the Metrodome in 2008. Buehrle has a career 21-11 record against the Twins, more wins than against any other opponent for the left-hander, including a 10-5 mark in Minneapolis.

home_pitcher_note: Perkins allowed five earned runs on eights hits in six innings in his last start, a 5-1 Twins loss to the Yankees. The rookie left-hander cruised through the contest's first four innings but surrendered two runs in the fifth and three in the sixth before being removed. Perkins will next take on the White Sox, against whom he received a no-decision on June 9, going 5 1/3 innings while giving up three earned runs in a 7-5 Minnesota loss in Chicago.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander earned rave reviews in his Major League debut on Wednesday by striking out seven over four innings, marking the highest total for a White Sox big league debut since Ravelo Manzanillo fanned eight on Sept. 25, 1988. Richard allowed four earned runs on seven hits over four innings, walking just one, but didn't get great support from his defense. He threw 50 of his 85 pitches for strikes, and the one-time University of Michigan quarterback did enough to earn a second start, at the Metrodome.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran right-hander was rocked early in his start Friday at Cleveland, allowing four runs in the first inning of the Twins' 5-4 loss. Had a potential RBI double by Jeff Bailey not instead hit the third-base umpire and resulted in a bizarre putout, the damage off Jackson might have been worse. But this outing still showed him making some big pitches in big situations. He will face the White Sox for the first time.

home_pitcher_note: It will be interesting to see how Buehrle comes back on three days rest after throwing a season-high 121 pitches in Wednesday's 3-2 loss to the Twins. But White Sox pitching coach Don Cooper said the earliest of plans has Buehrle working Sunday, if the White Sox still have not clinched or been eliminated. Buehrle allowed eighth hits and three runs on Wednesday, striking out three and walking four, as he battled his control all night. Buehrle has a 0-1 record and 9.22 ERA over three starts against the Indians this year, but he also features a 10-3 record with a 2.74 ERA at home.
away_pitcher_note: Cy Young Award favorite Cliff Lee was scratched from this start because of neck stiffness. The Sox will instead run up against Bullington, a former No. 1 Draft pick of the Pirates who was a reclamation project at Triple-A Buffalo in the second half of this season. Bullington (0-1, 5.59 ERA) has made two appearances for the Indians in September -- a spotty spot start against the Royals on Sept. 13 and an outstanding bit of long relief work Wednesday night in Boston, when he worked five scoreless innings. Lee getting scratched was probably welcome news to the Sox, against whom he was 1-0 with a 0.53 ERA in two starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Floyd almost stopped the bleeding for the White Sox again on Thursday night at the Metrodome, going in search of his 10th victory this season after a White Sox loss. Floyd allowed four runs on 11 hits over 5 2/3 innings, walking one and striking out four, but he managed to strand seven Minnesota runners. Floyd finished with a no-decision, when the bullpen couldn't hold a two-run lead. Floyd has a 2-0 record with a 4.24 ERA against Detroit this season and is 3-0 lifetime against the Tigers. Floyd will be pitching on three days' rest, having lost his last time in Kansas City following the short break.
away_pitcher_note: The rotation order just worked out for Garcia to be on turn for a possible Monday outing if the game was necessary. If it is, he'll be in the curious position of having a chance to either knock his former team out of the division title or force them into a one-game playoff. All in all, it's not a bad way to end a late-season comeback from shoulder surgery that cost him more than a year off the mound. Since he was planning on starting his winter ball campaign in his native Venezuela in a few weeks, the extra work won't be a big deal.

home_pitcher_note: Danks will be pitching on short rest, but he did not work very long on Friday against Cleveland, lasting four innings and allowing seven runs on seven hits. He threw 80 pitches in that game, which means he should still be relatively fresh come Tuesday. He's struggled since late August, posting a 4.91 ERA over his past seven starts. He earned a win in only one of those starts. Danks is 1-1 with a 7.91 in four starts against Minnesota this season.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn will take the hill for Tuesday's one-game tiebreaker in place of injured right-hander Kevin Slowey. Blackburn started the year 9-6 with a 3.60 ERA but he is 2-4 in his past nine starts with a 5.74 ERA. He's only gone more than five innings in four of those nine starts. However, he received the win in the Twins' 3-2 victory over the White Sox on Wednesday when he gave up two runs on eight hits and two walks over five innings. Blackburn is 2-2 with a 5.67 ERA in five starts against Chicago in 2008.

home_pitcher_note: Shields pitched one inning Sunday against the Tigers in a final tune-up before the playoffs and retired the side in order. The 26-year-old right-hander's best pitch has always been his changeup, but he also has a plus fastball and curve, and he's added a cutter that has helped him throw inside to left-handers. Shields enters the playoffs after pitching 215 innings for the second consecutive season, which is a testament to his style of pitching and his competitiveness. Unless something goes drastically wrong, Shields can be counted upon to give the team seven or more innings. Shields is 9-2 with a 2.59 ERA in 17 starts at Tropicana Field this season.
away_pitcher_note: Manager Ozzie Guillen announced that Vazquez will make the Game 1 start for the White Sox, pitching on four days' rest after pitching Saturday on short rest. Vazquez, has a 1-2 record and 3.54 ERA against the Rays this season, along with a 5-9 record and 5.10 ERA on the road.
summary: 2008-10-02 - Chicago White Sox (4) @ Tampa Bay Rays (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Kazmir lost his last start against the Tigers Sept. 25 when he allowed four home runs in five innings. The 24-year-old left-hander has struggled with his mechanics all season and has worked all season with little luck to gain command of his slider, which has historically been his best pitch. Without his slider, Kazmir has relied primarily on a fastball-changeup combination. Kazmir is 8-2 with a 2.90 ERA in 14 starts at Tropicana Field this season.
away_pitcher_note: Buehrle would be considered the staff ace, despite 17 wins from Gavin Floyd, and certainly has the most playoff experience among the four White Sox starters. But with a 4-9 record and 5.05 ERA on the road, compared to his 11-3 mark and 2.65 ERA at home, Buehrle might have been held back to Game 3 if not for Floyd and Danks being unable to work on such short rest. Pitching on Friday also would set up Buehrle to come back for a potential Game 5 on regular rest. Buehrle has a 0-1 record in three starts this season against Tampa Bay and carries a 5.54 ERA over two starts at Tropicana Field. Carlos Pena has five hits in 10 at-bats against Buehrle, and Pena is expected to play on Friday.
summary: 2008-10-03 - Chicago White Sox (2) @ Tampa Bay Rays (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: It will be difficult for Danks to match the best game pitched in his young career, after he held the Twins scoreless over eight innings on Tuesday in the 1-0 tiebreaker victory to win the American League Central. Danks will be coming back on regular rest, after making the first start on three days rest of his career. Danks has a 5-6 record with a 3.66 ERA at home this year, although he has held opposing hitters to a .238 average at U.S. Cellular Field. Danks was picked over Gavin Floyd for Game 3 because Tampa Bay struggles more against lefties, but Danks has a .264 average against with lefties, as opposed to .240 against righties. Danks is 2-1 with a miniscule 1.86 ERA against the Rays this season. He will be making his playoff debut.
away_pitcher_note: Garza started for the Rays  on Saturday against the Tigers, making his first start since Sept. 17, when he pitched against the Red Sox on short rest for the first time in his career. The 24-year-old right-hander was skipped in his next turn in an attempt to allow him to rejuvenate himself, and the plan seemed to work as Garza had electric stuff against the Tigers. Afterward, Garza reported that his arm felt great and he particularly liked his breaking stuff. Many on the team believe Garza has the best stuff on the Rays staff. He has a mid-90s fastball that sinks, a curve, a slider and a changeup.
summary: 2008-10-05 - Tampa Bay Rays (3) @ Chicago White Sox (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: In his first full season as part of the White Sox starting rotation, Floyd has become a true big-game pitcher for the South Siders. Floyd has nine wins after White Sox losses in 2008 and picked up an all-important victory over Detroit on Monday in a makeup game to force Tuesday's tiebreaker with the Twins. Floyd has a 10-3 record at home and has held right-handed hitters to a .226 average this season. Floyd not only missed out on facing Tampa Bay during the regular season but never has faced the Rays during his career. This start will be his first in the playoffs.
away_pitcher_note: On April 19, Sonnanstine spun a shutout at home against the White Sox, scattering three hits in the win. home_pitcher_note: For the past eight years, Buehrle has entered the season as arguably not the most talented pitcher in the White Sox starting rotation and ultimately was not their biggest winner. Yet, with the way Buehrle sets the tone through his tenaciousness and durability on the mound, the southpaw stands out as this team's clear-cut ace. Buehrle makes his seventh Opening Day start, with Jose Contreras getting the nod in 2006 standing as the only interruption to this impressive streak. He carries a 122-87 record with a 3.80 career ERA into the 2009 opener, not to mention a 19-8 lifetime mark against the Royals with a 3.48 ERA. Buehrle finished 3-2 against the Royals in 2008. By registering at least 10 wins, 30 starts and 200 innings for the eighth straight year, Buehrle became the only active pitcher in baseball to accomplish such a feat. His 68 victories at U.S. Cellular Field also stand as the stadium's top total. Buehrle enters the season needing just 17 starts to pass Joel Horlen for seventh place on the franchise all-time list and needs just 16 strikeouts to move him past Gary Peters and into the top five on the White Sox career ledger in that category. He has never been a hard thrower, but Buehrle relies on movement and pinpoint location to regularly get the job done.
away_pitcher_note: This is Meche's third straight Opening Day start. "It's just an exciting game. It's the only game like that all year long where it's so anticipated," he said. "The players are finally getting out of Spring Training and are finally getting to play in a game that counts. So I want the team to get off to a good start, and I'll do the best I can to make that happen." Meche revels in all the hoopla that surrounds the first game. "You walk out there and you see all the media, you see the amount of people camping out and tailgating before the game. And when I walk out of the dugout, to see all the fans that are already in the ballpark," he said. "Starting on the road in Detroit last year, you hear the fans getting on you -- 'Aw, you're gonna get it this year! You're gonna get it today' or whatever. And I know Chicago's going to be a little bit worse because the of the way the bullpen set-up is; they're literally right behind me in that little beer garden or whatever it is. But once the game starts, it's just another game. You kind of separate yourself from the fans even though it's going to be a packed house." Meche earned this start because he's been the rotation's strong man in his two KC seasons. He's never missed a start and he's grinded out a lot of innings. The Royals won both of Meche's first two Opening Day starts for them. It could be a good omen that his career record against the White Sox is 7-3 including 4-2 at the Cell.
summary: 2009-04-06 - Kansas City Royals @ Chicago White Sox (Postponed)

Floyd entered the 2008 season with eight career victories in 40 appearances, of which 29 were starts, but led the team with 17 wins in 33 starts. Floyd also held opponents hitless through seven innings twice, coming within two outs of no-hitting the Twins on May 6. His 206 1/3 innings pitched and 145 strikeouts also stood as career highs.
away_pitcher_note: Returning to full-time rotation duty after spending most of 2007 in the bullpen, Greinke established himself as extremely dependable in his 32 starts last season. He logged more than 200 innings and struck out 183. His ERA was the club's lowest since Kevin Appier's 3.40 in 1997. Greinke can crank it up to close to 98 mph when he wants to but he also uses good breaking pitches and changes speeds with sharp control.
summary: 2009-04-08 - Kansas City Royals (2) @ Chicago White Sox (0) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: There wasn't a more consistent starter among the White Sox rotation last year than the 23-year-old left-hander. Danks won 12 games but easily could have won five or six more, as he allowed two runs or fewer in 22 starts, tying Cy Young Award winner Cliff Lee for the most among American League pitchers. Danks made 19 quality starts and the White Sox went 18-15 with him on the mound. The southpaw made great usage of his cutter to post a 3.32 ERA, limit opposing hitters to a .246 average and fan 159 over 195 innings. One of his goals for 2009 is to top 200 innings pitcheed. Danks has a 1-0 career record against the Royals with a 3.28 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: What Davies has to prove early this season is that last September was no mirage. He made five starts in the month and came out 4-1 with a 2.27 ERA. Of course the entire team was on a roll, going 18-8. Davies began last season in Triple-A but battled his way back with a 6-2 record for Omaha and made 21 starts for Kansas City. The good news is he looked very good in Spring Training.
summary: 2009-04-09 - Kansas City Royals (2) @ Chicago White Sox (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Contreras' comeback from a ruptured left achilles tendon has been impressive. Contreras suffered the injury covering first base during a game against Boston on Aug. 9. Contreras bounced back from a rough 2007 campaign to finish above .500 and lower his ERA from 5.57 to 4.54. He attacks hitters from a couple of different angles to keep them off stride and was able to throw all of his pitches during his Spring Training recovery. Contreras has a 4-3 record with a 4.13 ERA against the Twins and has a lifetime 26-20 mark with a 4.22 ERA at U.S. Cellular Field.
away_pitcher_note: Considered on the bubble for a roster spot heading into the final week of spring, Dickey earned the No. 5 spot in the rotation after Scott Baker was placed on the 15-day disabled list. The knuckleballer is coming off perhaps his best spring, having posted a 2.04 ERA in 11 appearances. That included striking out 18 batters in his 17 2/3 innings. A key to Dickey's success has been a more consistent knuckleball, which he worked on this past winter with the legendary Phil Niekro. Now the hope of the Twins and Dickey is that he can translate the improved pitch into regular season success.

home_pitcher_note: Colon was as durable as any starter on the White Sox staff when he threw nine complete games for the team back in 2003. But after having bone chips removed from his pitching elbow in October, the White Sox don't expect a lot of nine-inning efforts from the burly right-hander. Colon made seven starts for the Red Sox last year but has made just 35 starts over the past three seasons combined. Colon's velocity topped out in the low 90s during his Cactus League starts.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano didn't walk away with a win in his first career Opening Day outing, but the Twins were pleased with what they saw from the left-hander. He was able to pitch seven innings, allowing four runs on four hits. His trouble was limited to a couple of mistake pitches, including a hanging slider that he left up for Ken Griffey Jr. to hit for a home run. Liriano will face his first road test of the season when he takes on the White Sox at U.S. Cellular Field. The lefty is 0-1 with a 5.14 ERA in two contests there.

home_pitcher_note: It was not a typical start for Buehrle, as he was consistently behind Royals' hitters and had to work his way out of trouble in each of five innings pitched during his seventh Opening Day trip to the mound. By the time Clayton Richard replaced Buehrle, the White Sox ace had walked three, hit two and given up six hits, but yielded just two earned runs. Buehrle threw 97 pitches, with just 58 of them going for strikes. Buehrle blamed his Opening Day woes on being too amped up and overthrowing instead of just trying to hit his spots. He has the most wins in the history of U.S. Cellular Field at 68 and holds a 21-13 career mark against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: It wasn't the prettiest of starts for Blackburn in his first outing of the year against the Mariners. The right-hander had to battle through five innings, giving up four runs on eight hits. The feeling of the Twins staff was that the numbers were a tad worse than Blackburn's actual performance as many of the hits were bloopers or jammed shots. But the pitcher said that he was going to work between starts on keeping his ball down in the zone as some of his pitches were a little high -- although that was perhaps a result of some first-outing jitters. In his next start, Blackburn will return to Chicago, where he delivered a gem of a performance in the club's 1-0 loss to the White Sox in a one-game tiebreaker for the AL Central title last September.

home_pitcher_note: Opening the season in a Major League rotation for the first time in his career, Miner recovered from four straight baserunners to open his season debut Wednesday at Toronto and tossed 5 2/3 innings of one-run ball, collecting Detroit's first win of the year in the process. Now he returns home to Comerica Park, where his career 5.28 ERA is more than two full runs higher than his 3.14 mark on the road. Opponents have batted .301 against him at home compared with .234 everywhere else.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander looked every bit as dominant during his first start of 2009 as his stellar Spring Training projected him to be. Floyd worked seven innings, fanning nine and walking two, while giving up two runs on six hits. Those two runs were two too many against the Royals, as Zack Greinke was just a little bit better. Floyd has made a living out of manhandling the Tigers, posting a 3-0 record with a 3.68 ERA against the Tigers in a 2008 to boost his career mark to 4-0. He holds a 2-0 record with a 2.63 ERA at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello's Major League debut Thursday at Toronto turned on a pair of home runs that sent him to defeat. However, he still gave a good look at the poise and pitching acumen that convinced the Tigers he could handle the jump from Class A ball to the Majors at the age of 20. Now he'll try to build off that outing with the extra challenge of facing a powerful White Sox known for chewing up young Tigers pitchers over the last few years, such as Justin Verlander.
away_pitcher_note: Although Danks felt as if he wasn't efficient enough with his 95 pitches, the southpaw still threw six scoreless innings during Thursday's loss to the Royals. Danks gave up just three singles, while walking three and striking out five. He also had to pitch out of a bases-loaded, one-out jam in the third, courtesy of Mark Teahen's line-drive double play. The southpaw posted a 2-0 record with a 2.41 ERA against the Tigers in 2008 and has a 2-1 career mark against Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: Any questions on whether last year's Tigers surprise story has the capability to repeat or better his breakout 2008 season seemingly were answered Friday, when Galarraga dominated the previously scorching Rangers offense for seven innings of one-run ball. His eight strikeouts marked a career high, and the Rangers that did hit the ball never made good contact, limited to five singles and a slew of groundouts. He ended up being the perfect starter for the always-intense home opener in Detroit, and he'll close out the opening homestand against the only division opponent he didn't start against last year. His lone meeting with the White Sox was his ill-fated relief appearance in the season's final game.
away_pitcher_note: It certainly wasn't a dominant effort for Contreras in his first start since rupturing his left Achilles tendon back on Aug. 9, 2008. But the Twins didn't exactly crush the right-hander, a performance somewhere in between that was somewhat expected from the veteran. Contreras gave up four earned runs on seven hits, including Joe Crede's home run, over five innings. He walked three, struck out three and threw 86 pitches. But most importantly, Contreras felt healthy after his first regular-season test. Contreras has an 8-8 lifetime record against Detroit and a 4-4 mark at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Niemann made his first start of the season against the Orioles on Saturday night and got off to a less-than-auspicious beginning when he allowed five runs in the first inning, most of which came via a Melvin Mora grand slam. He did settle in to pitch four scoreless innings before getting lifted with one out in the fifth, but he still took the loss. Niemann has made one career start against the White Sox and is 0-1 with a 13.50 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Although Danks felt as if he wasn't efficient enough with his 95 pitches, the southpaw still threw six scoreless innings during Thursday's loss to the Royals. Danks gave up just three singles, while walking three and striking out five. He also had to pitch out of a bases-loaded, one-out jam in the third, courtesy of Mark Teahen's line-drive double play. Danks posted a 2-1 record with a 1.86 ERA against the Rays in 2008 and has a 3-1 career mark against Tampa Bay.

Garza is 1-1 with a 4.97 ERA in three career starts against the White Sox.
away_pitcher_note: Floyd gave up two runs and struck out nine over seven innings in his first start this season, but suffered the loss at home to Kansas City. Floyd struck out two and gave up six runs, throwing just 49 of his 98 pitches for strikes in improving to 5-0 lifetime against the Tigers and 3-0 at Comerica Park. away_pitcher_note: The final numbers over 5 1/3 innings might not indicate a solid start for the veteran right-hander in Detroit on Wednesday afternoon, but Contreras definitely took a step up from his first trip to the mound this season. Contreras pitched four scoreless innings before giving up two runs in the fifth via a two-out single from Placido Polanco on a 1-2 pitch, and then was charged with three more in the sixth, although only four of the five runs were earned. Contreras struck out four, walked two and threw 59 of his 96 pitches for strikes in the loss to the Tigers. Contreras posted a 2-0 record with a 1.32 ERA against the Orioles last year and has a 5-4 record with a 4.64 ERA lifetime against Baltimore. Contreras has a 2-1 mark at Camden Yards.

home_pitcher_note: In Baltimore's rotation, there's Jeremy Guthrie and everyone else. Only one Orioles pitcher has completed six innings this year, and that would be Guthrie, who's done it twice. Baltimore's staff ace got knocked out early in his last start, though, allowing eight runs against the Red Sox. Only five of those runs were earned, but Guthrie and the Orioles surrendered a seven-run lead against Boston. Still, Baltimore will be hotly anticipating his next outing, which comes against the White Sox at home.
away_pitcher_note: It might be based on only two 2009 starts, but factoring in last year's season-long dominance, Danks truly has risen to elite status as a starter. The left-hander limited the Rays to one run on two hits over six innings in Thursday's 3-2 victory, with that run coming on Carlos Pena's fifth home run, while fanning eight and walking four. For the season, Danks has given up just that one run on five hits over 12 innings, while striking out 13 and walking seven. He pitched on six days' rest at Tropicana Field and will have five days before this next start courtesy of Monday's off-day. Danks has a 1-2 mark and a 5.94 ERA lifetime against the Orioles and is 0-1 with a 9.00 ERA at Camden Yards.

away_pitcher_note: Duke had been charged with no more than one run in five of his previous seven starts entering his last outing against Colorado on May 17. To his credit, Duke didn't let the one bad inning shake him, and he kept his team in the game. Duke has no record in his career against the White Sox, with a 6.75 ERA in two appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Richard tossed his best outing of the year against the Blue Jays in his last start -- no small feat given that the Jays are one of the top offensive teams in baseball. The southpaw reeled off seven strong innings, allowing two runs (one earned) on three hits. He walked three, struck out three and exhausted 94 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Manager John Russell may have described it best when he characterized Ohlendorf's last start as uneven. It featured three straight innings in which he faced the minimum, but it also included a five-run inning by Washington's offense. Ohlendorf never got his off-speed pitches in sync and left too many balls out over the plate. While he has been fairly consistent all season, he still needs to improve his efforts in getting ahead of hitters and in quickening his pace early in the start. Ohlendorf has made one career appearance against the White Sox and it wasn't pretty. The righty allowed five earned runs on five hits in two innings of relief.

home_pitcher_note: After watching his personal-best five-game winning streak come to an end last Wednesday in Cleveland, Buehrle returned to his winning ways with a stellar effort on five days rest against the Twins at home on Tuesday. The left-hander allowed one earned run on eight hits over seven innings, striking out three and not issuing a walk. He threw 62 of his 101 pitches for strikes and pitched out of two scoring threats posed by the Twins, limiting Minnesota to just one unearned run. Buehrle has a 3-0 career record against the Pirates with a 1.96 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Karsten's last start featured five solid innings and one forgettable sixth inning, in which Karstens allowed three runs on four hits. He continues to work through some mechanical adjustments and is throwing three bullpen sessions in between starts (as opposed to the normal one) to help him expedite the process. Still, it seems that he can't stay away from having one bad inning in which his pitches are consistently up in the zone. Karstens' only career appearance against the White Sox resulted in a loss after the righty allowed three runs on five hits in 3 1/3 innings of relief.

home_pitcher_note: Santana improved in his second start of the season, going 6 2/3 innings and throwing 95 pitches while only giving up one run on five hits. Unfortunately for the right-hander, who touched 93 mph as he ramps his velocity back up after missing most of the first two months because of a right elbow sprain, his team didn't score any runs in a 1-0 defeat. Santana said he felt a lot better with his mechanics and rhythm and that his location was much better than in his first 2009 outing, when he gave up three runs on seven hits in five innings against the Boston Red Sox on May 14.
away_pitcher_note: Danks returned to his winning ways by allowing just two earned runs over 5 2/3 innings during a 7-4 victory over the Twins on Wednesday, the first win for Danks since April 22 at Baltimore and the first at U.S. Cellular Field since Sept. 30, 2008 in the Blackout AL Central playoff game against the Twins. Danks struck out seven, walked three and threw 70 of his 111 pitches for strikes. The left-hander also was touched for Michael Cuddyer's two-run home run in the sixth, which pretty much brought an end to his night. He has a career 0-1 record against the Angels in three starts, with a 2.16 ERA, including 6 1/3 scoreless innings thrown at Angel Stadium in just one start.
summary: 2009-05-25 - Chicago White Sox (17) @ Los Angeles Angels (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Back in All-Star form, Saunders rebounded from his first ineffective outing in Texas with a dominant effort in Seattle, shutting out the Mariners across seven innings on four hits, the bullpen preserving the shutout. Saunders struck out three and walked three, allowing only one runner to reach third base. Saunders is 2-1 in four career starts against the White Sox with a 3.96 ERA. He is 2-1 at home with a 2.93 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Colon struggled in his shortest outing of the season in a loss against the Twins on Thursday. He threw just two innings and 61 pitches, surrendering back-to-back home runs in a seven-run second inning. All seven of those runs were unearned because of an error, but Colon still allowed seven hits in the contest. Colon did not pitch more than two innings in a start for just the eighth time in 321 career starts.
summary: 2009-05-26 - Chicago White Sox (4) @ Los Angeles Angels (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Weaver continued to pitch superbly against the Dodgers but once again had nothing to show for it, in terms of a decision. He pitched out of trouble repeatedly in holding the Dodgers to one run across five innings, yielding eight hits and three walks while striking out three. Weaver got ground-ball outs when he needed to and showed his competitive nature in frustrating the Dodgers. Weaver has dominated the White Sox throughout his career. He's 3-0 in four starts, having allowed one earned run in 26 2/3 innings -- a 0.34 ERA. He's 3-0 with a 1.23 ERA in five home starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: Floyd tossed his best game of the season against the Pirates in a 2-0 victory on Friday. He had command of all four of his pitches -- fastball, changeup, curveball and cutter -- tossing a season-high eight innings and allowing two hits while striking out eight. In doing so, Floyd won his first start in six attempts. Floyd also lowered his ERA from 7.71 to 6.54.
summary: 2009-05-27 - Chicago White Sox (1) @ Los Angeles Angels (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Bannister is really clicking since being recalled from Triple-A, using a dazzling cutter to mystify batters. In his last outing at St. Louis, Bannister worked six innings for the victory, giving up seven hits that included six singles and a double. The Royals have won six of the seven games he's started this season. Among the starters, only Zack Greinke has a better record and ERA. This is his first shot at the White Sox this year; he's 2-3 with a 7.66 ERA against them in his career but that includes a 0-2 mark in four games last year.
away_pitcher_note: Richard, making just his third start of the season, threw 107 pitches in another strong effort on Saturday, a 4-0 victory over the Pirates. Richard struck out a career-high eight batters in six innings, allowing four hits. He lowered his ERA from 4.33 to 3.55. Richard had made 12 relief appearances this season before being called upon to start on May 12 against the Indians.
summary: 2009-05-29 - Chicago White Sox (11) @ Kansas City Royals (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Meche had his shortest outing of the season in his last start, lasting just 2 1/3 innings in a loss to the Tigers. Meche, who has been battling a tight lower back, said his body felt fine after losing for the third time in four starts. According to Meche, he just wasn't pitching well enough to win. It was a tough setback for Meche, who was coming off a quality start against Cleveland on May 20, when he allowed just two runs in six innings but drew a no-decision. Meche's last victory came at Minnesota on May 3, but he does have one solid outing against the White Sox already. He pitched seven innings and allowed one run in a no-decision on Opening Day in Chicago.
away_pitcher_note: Buehrle gave up a season-high 12 hits Sunday against the Pirates but left the game with a 3-1 lead.
