Floyd has faced Oakland once this season, going seven innings in a 6-2 win. He allowed two runs on just four hits.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill achieved his longest outing since going seven innings on July 22, but it wasn't enough to keep him from suffering his 12th loss of the season. The rookie allowed three earned runs on eight hits, but issued no walks in his team's 3-2 loss to the Orioles.
away_pitcher_note: Danks finally broke out of a recent mini-slump with one of his best outings of the season, allowing one run in eight innings against the Mariners. He was efficient, throwing only 98 pitches, and struck out eight batters in the process. The start was especially important because Chicago starters had struggled the last time through the rotation. Danks is 4-0 lifetime against Oakland with a 1.38 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle is winless in four starts since his perfect game on July 23 against the Rays, but his most recent outing was another gem. The veteran lefty threw a six-hitter over eight shutout innings but took a no-decision, as the game went 14 innings. Buehrle is 20-8 with a 3.41 ERA lifetime against the Kansas City Royals. He's beaten only the Minnesota Twins (23-15) more often.
away_pitcher_note: Bannister has had two rough starts since seven brilliant shutout innings at Tampa Bay. He's given up seven runs to Oakland and seven more to Minnesota and his ERA has jumped from 3.59 to over the 4.00 mark. Bannister has prospered this season with a lot of movement on his pitches, notably his cutter, and he says that life just hasn't been there in his last two outings. Perhaps his arm is weary; if so, he resolved to rest it more before he faces the White Sox. He's faced them twice this season, splitting two decisions. They cuffed him around the first time, but he stopped them on two runs in six innings last time.
summary: 2009-08-17 - Kansas City Royals (7) @ Chicago White Sox (8) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Garcia hasn't pitched in the Major Leagues since last September as a member of the Detroit Tigers, but the White Sox are hoping to capture a glimpse of the Garcia who led them to the 2005 World Series championship. He's 0-3 with a 6.35 ERA in three Triple-A starts this season and 8-11 with a 6.12 ERA lifetime against the Royals.
away_pitcher_note: Returning after missing more than a month and at least four starts because of back problems, Meche pitched five innings last Thursday at Minnesota and emerged with a victory. For the first four innings, he filled the strike zone and held the Twins to just one run although he did give up a three-run homer to Joe Mauer in the fifth. The good news was that there was no recurrence of his back problems. This year against the White Sox, Meche has no decisions in two starts although he went seven innings each time and had a 1.94 ERA. And he's 7-3 against them in his career.
summary: 2009-08-18 - Kansas City Royals (5) @ Chicago White Sox (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, at Oakland on Friday night, Contreras allowed two hits in his first 3 1/3 innings before the walls caved in on him. He gave up seven runs on six hits over his final nine hitters and is now winless over his past six starts. Contreras' statistics look dreadful, but White Sox manager Ozzie Guillen said the veteran right-hander will make his regular start.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Greinke pitched well enough to win, posting seven shutout innings against the Tigers on Friday night, but Jarrod Washburn was just as tough. Greinke took a no-decision as the Tigers won in the ninth on a walk-off homer. Greinke gave up just three hits, and while he walked four batters, his most all season, the right-hander wasn't all that concerned with his control. For the most part, he felt that he was on target. He notched seven strikeouts and now has 174 in 166 1/3 innings this season. This will be Greinke's fifth start against the White Sox this season; he's 2-1 with one no-decision and a 1.61 ERA against them.
summary: 2009-08-19 - Kansas City Royals (2) @ Chicago White Sox (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Floyd has become perhaps Chicago's most reliable starter. He's 7-2 over his past 14 starts and has allowed one earned run or fewer in nine of those outings. He pitched seven solid innings against the A's on Saturday, giving up a run on eight hits while walking two and striking out eight. Floyd is 1-0 with a 1.29 ERA in two career starts against the Orioles.
away_pitcher_note: Guthrie continued to struggle in the opening innings on Sunday, giving up three earned runs in the first inning against the Angels. Guthrie lasted 5 2/3 innings, allowing 10 hits and issuing two walks, but picked up the no-decision in Baltimore's 17-8 loss in 13 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Danks put together his second successive solid start in a no-decision against the A's on Sunday, allowing two runs on eight hits in 7 1/3 innings. He left with the lead, but an inherited runner scored to take away the decision. Danks hasn't performed nearly at well at home lately, but he did beat the Orioles on July 17 and is 3-2 with a 4.21 ERA lifetime against them.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez fell victim to the long ball in his last start, giving up three home runs, five runs overall, to fall to 4-5 this season. Hernandez lasted 5 1/3 innings, issuing four walks with one strikeout.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander looked in position to pick up his first victory since throwing the 18th perfect game in Major League history on July 23 against Tampa Bay, but Scott Linebrink's blown save in the eighth kept Buehrle winless during that stretch. Buehrle gave up four runs on nine hits in six innings against the Royals, walking two and not recording a strikeout. Since making history, Buehrle has a 0-3 record with a 5.85 ERA and has allowed 43 hits in 32 1/3 innings covering five starts. Buehrle's Major League-record streak of 45 straight batters retired began with the last out recorded of his last start against the Orioles. He has a 1-0 record against the Orioles this season and is 5-2 lifetime when facing Baltimore.
away_pitcher_note: Berken fell for the 11th time in his last 12 starts since winning his Major League debut in late May, and on paper his start vs. Tampa Bay looks like one of his worst. He allowed a season-high 11 hits, five runs, and three home runs in 5 2/3 innings to the Rays. But in reality, Berken had good stuff and showed strong poise and command while working in and out of trouble. He allowed two solo home runs in the sixth inning which ended his outing, and has now given up 10 home runs in his last seven starts after allowing three in his first nine. His ERA is now over 9.00 on the road.

home_pitcher_note: The third time proved to be the charm for Buchholz last Wednesday in Toronto as the right-hander bested Blue Jays ace Roy Halladay after being outdueled by the Yankees' CC Sabathia and the Tigers' Justin Verlander in his previous two outings. Buchholz fired six innings of one-run ball at Rogers Centre, striking out four to record his third straight quality start after failing to log six innings in his first four appearances of 2009. The 25-year-old did not fare well against the White Sox last Aug. 10 at U.S. Celluar Field, yielding five runs on seven hits over three innings.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, on Wednesday afternoon, Contreras outdueled Royals ace Zack Greinke to pick up a victory. During that run, he has finished just two seasons with an ERA over 4.00. Buehrle posted a 13-10 record and a 3.84 ERA last season, which also included the second perfect game hurled by a White Sox pitcher, as well as a Major League record 45 straight batters retired. Westbrook's last big league start was May 28, 2008, against, coincidentally enough, the White Sox. He proved his health in camp, and his velocity is intact, but his ability to command the strike zone was a bit inconsistent. Westbrook, who also started on Opening Day in 2005, is 8-11 with a 4.94 ERA in 27 career appearances against the Sox. He is 5-5 with a 4.46 ERA in 13 career appearances at U.S. Cellular Field.

home_pitcher_note: The White Sox basically were out of contention by the time Peavy got close to healthy last year, so the right-hander didn't have to even take the mound in mid-September. Peavy made three starts, won all three and finished with a 1.35 ERA, giving up 11 hits and striking out 18 in 20 innings. Now, Peavy returns with a healthy right ankle and a healthy pitching elbow, which he took a line drive off of during a Minor League rehab start last year, confident he will be leading a rotation with the possibility of pushing the White Sox to a World Series title. Peavy has a 95-68 career record, although all but these three wins have come against National League competition. He was considered for the Opening Day start but pushed for Buehrle to get the nod and the franchise record. Peavy is 1-1 against the Indians and 2-0 at U.S. Cellular.
away_pitcher_note: Who is going to show up for the Indians in the No. 2 spot of their rotation this season? The 19-win Carmona of 2007, the walk-prone Carmona of 2008 and '09 or something in between? Carmona, who was demoted to the Minors last season, showed flashes of his '07 self in winter ball and throughout Spring Training camp. He was aggressive in the strike zone, efficient with his pitches and composed on the mound. Now, we'll see if he can take that into the regular season. Carmona is 4-3 with a 4.50 ERA in 10 career appearances against the Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Floyd has returned healthy after leaving a game on Sept. 16 with a sore left hip and not pitching the remainder of the 2009 season. He takes the third spot in the rotation, with the White Sox choosing to throw John Danks against the plethora of left-handed hitters featured by the Twins in the weekend series. Floyd had an 11-11 mark and 4.06 ERA in 2009 but finished strong by lowering his ERA from 4.44 before the All-Star Break to 3.49 after it. Since 2008, Floyd ranks second among AL right-handers in opponents average against with a .242 mark, sits in a tie for sixth with 28 victories and his 38 quality starts leave him seventh. Floyd has a 4-2 career record with a 4.30 ERA against the Indians and has a 16-9 mark at U.S. Cellular.
away_pitcher_note: The big-bodied Masterson has Major League stuff, but can he be effective as a Major League starter? Masterson was erratic in spring camp and needs to show improvement with his changeup if he's going to be successful as a starter, and against left-handers in particular. Masterson is 0-1 with a 1.53 ERA in five career appearances, including two starts, against the Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Moving Danks to the fourth spot in the rotation gives the White Sox two left-handers to throw in the first weekend of the season against the Twins' left-handed-laden lineup. He brings in a 4-5 career record against Minnesota and has a 13-19 mark at U.S. Cellular.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off a strong winter ball performance in the Dominican Republic, Liriano was able to carry that success into Spring Training and beat out Brian Duensing for the fifth starter's spot. That will begin with Liriano opening up the series against the White Sox in Chicago. Liriano is 0-3 with an 8.50 ERA in three career starts at U.S. Cellular Field.

Garcia finished 3-2 with a 3.66 ERA in his final six starts of the year. The right-hander sits 40 games over .500 for his career, at 121-81, and has a 9-5 record with a 3.83 ERA against the Twins. away_pitcher_note: Baker got off to a shaky start in his first outing of the season, giving up four runs on five hits over 4 2/3 innings. One thing that the starter can work on is making better two-strike pitches; he was hurt by them against veteran hitters like Hideki Matsui. Buehrle also made what just might be the defensive play of the year on the first day of the season, deflecting a Lou Marson fifth-inning grounder with his left shin on a hockey goalie-like kick-save and then scooping it with his glove with a no-look flip between his legs to first baseman Paul Konerko, who caught it barehanded for the out.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn didn’t appear to show any effects in his first start of being limited this spring by some right knee soreness. Blackburn allowed just three runs on eight hits over 6 2/3 innings, striking out four and walking four in the contest. Blackburn said that he and catcher Joe Mauer will continue to work on making sure they have a good handle on his sinker’s movement. Next up, Blackburn will face the White Sox in Chicago. He is 2-4 with a 3.48 ERA in seven career starts at U.S. Cellular Field.

Floyd allowed nine hits, two walks and four earned runs while striking out five in six innings. The Blue Jays have been Floyd's most difficult opponent and Tuesday's loss  put him at 0-4 with a 7.22 ERA in five games against them. In this third start of  the season he will face the team he faced in his opening start, the Indians. He did not figure in the decision in the White Sox 5-3 loss on April 8. Floyd allowed two runs on five hits over six innings while striking out seven and walking three. He left the game with the White Sox trailing, 2-1. Since joining the White Sox in 2007, he is 4-2 against the Indians and 2-1 with a  5.79 ERA in Cleveland. Last year, Floyd generally was  much better pitching at home, where his ERA was 2.47, compared to 5.47 on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Danks used his changeup to his advantage when he two-hit the Blue Jays over seven innings in his second start of the season, an 11-1 victory. He walked three and struck out six with 65 strikes out of 103 pitches. It was an impressive outing against a team he had never lasted more than five innings against previously, let alone beat them -- and in a park where the White Sox have had problems. He is 4-1 with a 2.67 ERA in five career starts against the Rays, but all those wins were at Tropicana Field, where he has a 2.25 ERA in four starts.
away_pitcher_note: On Wednesday against the Orioles, Price put forth his second dominating performance in as many starts in 2010. The No. 1 pick of the 2007 June Draft has shown a lot of improvement in his fastball command, which has made his slider and curve even more effective. Price allowed just one run on four hits in seven innings against the Orioles with seven strikeouts and two walks. Of the 103 pitches he threw, 70 were for strikes. Typical of Price, he was not satisfied with his outing, in particular the walks. Price is 0-1 with a 6.00 ERA in one career start against the White Sox, which came at U.S. Cellular Field.
summary: 2010-04-20 - Tampa Bay Rays (1) @ Chicago White Sox (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle gave the White Sox a chance to win in his third start of the season, but the offense didn't come through to prevent a 6-2 Cleveland victory on Friday night at Progressive Field. Buehrle had a stretch of 17 2/3 consecutive scoreless innings thrown against the Indians, dating back to 2009, come to an end during a three-run fourth inning, and allowed three earned runs on six hits over six innings. Buehrle fanned three but lamented his four walks, including two to lead off innings, both of whom came around to score. Buehrle made history the last time he faced the Rays, throwing the 18th perfect game in big league history on July 23, 2009, at U.S. Cellular. It was the second of Buehrle's two career no-hitters. He will be pitching on regular rest with the White Sox decision to give Freddy Garcia a couple of extra days and bypass his next start.
away_pitcher_note: Davis will be making his third start of the season after a solid outing against the Red Sox on Friday night. The right-hander received a no-decision on the heels of a performance that saw him allow one run on two hits in five innings of work in the game that eventually was suspended. Davis became the third rookie in Rays history to allow two hits or less in an outing of five innings or more against the Red Sox. Davis showed quality stuff, but the Red Sox were able to push up his pitch count -- 104 pitches -- to force an early exodus. Davis has great command of his pitches and isn't afraid to throw a breaking ball in any situation. Davis will be making his first career start against the White Sox.
summary: 2010-04-21 - Tampa Bay Rays (12) @ Chicago White Sox (0) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: With the White Sox bypassing Freddy Garcia's next turn in the rotation, Peavy comes back on regular rest to throw in Thursday's series finale against the Rays. The right-hander bounced back from a rough outing in Toronto at the start of this seven-game road trip to give up just two runs on four hits over 7 1/3 innings. Unfortunately for Peavy, the last batter he faced, in Asdrubal Cabrera, hit a game-tying home run off of him in the eighth inning on his 109th pitch of the game. Peavy struck out three and walked three. Peavy has a 1-0 career record against the Rays and has a 2-0 mark at U.S. Cellular Field.
away_pitcher_note: Shields went 6 2/3 innings against the Red Sox on Saturday night to pick up his first win of the season and first career win at Fenway Park. The right-hander remained in the game longer than normal -- throwing a career-high 121 pitches -- to help an ailing bullpen, which cost him some additional runs, but he ultimately achieved his purpose. The 28-year-old right-hander is the old man of a young Rays staff and serves as a leader at the top of the rotation. He has built a reputation as a pitcher who will do whatever is necessary to get his team into the seventh or eighth innings -- evidenced by three consecutive seasons with 215 innings pitched. He is a master at using his fastball command to set up one of the best changeups in baseball. Shields is 1-1 with a 4.50 ERA in five career starts against the White Sox; he is 0-0 with a 3.95 ERA in two starts at U.S. Cellular Field.
summary: 2010-04-22 - Tampa Bay Rays (10) @ Chicago White Sox (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: To classify Floyd's brief 51-pitch trip to the mound on Sunday in Cleveland as one of the worst in his successful career would be an understatement. Floyd faced 13 batters in one-plus innings and retired only three. In contrast, reliever Tony Pena came into the contest with a runner on first and nobody out and needed one pitch to retire two in the second on a double play. Floyd gave up seven runs on six hits, including Shin-Soo Choo's grand slam, walking four and striking out two. Floyd will be working on normal four days rest when he opens the weekend series against Seattle. The right-hander has a 1-4 record with a lofty 7.47 ERA over six starts and eight games pitched in total against the Mariners, but Floyd does hold a 16-9 lifetime record at U.S. Cellular Field.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander pitched well enough to win his first game of the season in his last outing, holding the Tigers to two runs over six-plus innings -- a quality start -- but had to settle for a no-decision in his duel against Detroit ace Justin Verlander. A breaking ball that ended up in Magglio Ordonez's wheelhouse was the first hit Rowland-Smith surrendered. Two of the four hits he allowed were for extra bases and he struck out a season-high three. Rowland-Smith is 1-0 with a 1.08 ERA in two career appearances, including one start, against the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: The term used for the rotation change involving Garcia this weeks is not that he is being skipped but instead Garcia will receive a couple of extra days in between starts. With Garcia's regular turn being pushed back from Wednesday to Saturday, the veteran will have an eight-day respite and the front four of the rotation will stay on their regular rest. Garcia needs to produce a far better showing than his last trip to the mound, when Toronto tattooed him from seven runs on eight hits in three-plus innings. Garcia has allowed 11 hits and walked eight over 10 innings this season, while fanning seven. The one-time ace of the Seattle staff will be making start No. 8 against his old team, entering with a 3-3 ledger and a 6.04 ERA when facing the Mariners. Garcia has a 47-20 career record in day games.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander's confidence is at an all-time high following a best-of-his-career start against the Orioles. Fister took a no-hitter into the seventh inning before settling for a three-hitter and second consecutive win. The 6-foot-8 hurler throws over the top on a downward plane, giving his fastball a late break, which makes it difficult for hitters to center the ball. Though not overpowering, topping out at about 92 mph, he changes speed effectively and uses a changeup and sharp-breaking curve to keep hitters honest. He is developing an excellent working relationship with catcher Rob Johnson, allowing just one earned run in their two games together. Fister has made one previous start against the White Sox, holding them to one hit over six scoreless innings in a no-decision outing last season.

home_pitcher_note: The southpaw stopped the proverbial bleeding for the White Sox on Tuesday night, with his stellar start ending a four-game losing streak for his team and cutting short Tampa Bay's seven-game winning streak. Danks allowed two hits and two walks over eight innings, striking out nine in a tremendous 113-pitch effort. He had his cutter working well in the early innings, used his changeup once the Tampa Bay order turned over and then felt comfortable throwing any of his four pitches for a strike later in the game. Danks has given up just four hits and two earned runs over his last 15 innings. He has a 1-4 record and 5.00 ERA lifetime against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty is coming off one of the best outings of his year-plus career with the Mariners, holding the Orioles to three hits and one run over seven innings at Safeco Field last Tuesday night. Finally completely healthy after hip surgery almost two years ago, he has combined power with precision to post back-to-back quality starts and his strikeout-walk ratio (16-3) is outstanding. He has mastered the changeup, which has made his fastball look faster than it actually is, but hitters have a difficult time with it. Vargas is making a strong bid to stay in the rotation when Cliff Lee returns on April 30. He has faced the White Sox only once in his career, a two-thirds inning relief stint.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson won his first career game as a starter on Thursday, throwing 6 2/3 scoreless innings to lead the Rangers to a 3-0 victory. It marked the first time a Texas starter has thrown at least 6 2/3 scoreless innings at Fenway Park since Kenny Rogers threw seven scoreless on July 16, 1995. Wilson has also started the season with three consecutive quality starts and will attempt to become the first Rangers starter with four in a row since 1993, when both Brown and Charlie Leibrandt did it. In 10 lifetime appearances against the White Sox, Wilson has a 3.65 ERA with 10 strikeouts. In three appearances against them last year, Wilson threw three scoreless innings and allowed only two hits with two strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: The final line for Buehrle during Wednesday's 12-0 loss to the Rays doesn't look very impressive. The southpaw gave up six runs on nine hits over 4 2/3 innings, striking out four and walking one. But of the nine hits Buehrle allowed, six were of the broken-bat or bloop variety. They all count the same, though, as Buehrle suffered the setback in his shortest outing of the season. Buehrle has a dominant 11-3 record with a 2.93 ERA against the Rangers, marking his most wins against a team outside of the American League Central. Buehrle also has a 4-1 record at Rangers Ballpark.

home_pitcher_note: Harden has struggled of late, as he has pitched five-plus innings only once in his first four starts this season. On Friday against Detroit, Harden lasted only 4 1/3 innings, allowing two runs (both earned) on six hits with five strikeouts and four walks. Harden has also issued 18 walks in 17 2/3 innings this season. Despite his early struggles, the Rangers intend to stick with Harden for the foreseeable future. "We've just got to figure out a way to get Rich to be more conservative with his pitches," Rangers manager Ron Washington said. "Rich is capable of winning at the Major League level." Harden will try to pick up his first win in a Rangers uniform against the White Sox, whom he is 3-3 with a 3.00 ERA in seven lifetime starts.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander took a walk on the wild side during Thursday's 10-2 loss to the Rays, issuing a career-worst seven walks over 4 1/3 innings, while throwing 108 pitches. Peavy gave up seven runs on seven hits, suffering his first defeat in seven starts with the White Sox. One bright spot, according to Peavy, was how changes made in his mechanics between his last start and this start resulted in a rise in velocity and the best stuff he has felt he possessed all season. He simply needs to harness that stuff within the zone. Peavy has never faced the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman struggled in his last start, lasting only 3 2/3 innings, allowing eight runs (four earned) on eight hits with four walks and a strikeout in a losing effort against Detroit on Saturday. It marked his second straight loss, as he went only 2 1/3, allowing four runs on seven hits against the Yankees on April 17. After Saturday's game, Feldman said he needed to work on keeping his pitch count low after throwing 93 pitches. In seven lifetime appearances, including two starts, against the White Sox, Feldman is 1-1 with a 4.11 ERA. In his one start against Chicago last year, Feldman went 5 2/3 innings and allowed three runs on three hits with three strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander pitched far better than his last trip to the mound Sunday in Cleveland. But after giving up seven runs without retiring a batter in the second at Progressive Field, it couldn't have been much worse as Floyd stated. Floyd worked 6 1/3 innings against the Mariners on Friday in Chicago, allowing five runs on seven hits, while striking out four and walking three. Three of those runs scored when Jose Lopez hit a two-out grand slam off of reliever J.J. Putz in the seventh, erasing a chance for Floyd to pick up his first victory. Floyd has a 0-1 career record against the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Angels manager Mike Scioscia opined that Pettitte is pitching "the best we've ever seen him, probably ever" after his last start. The Elias Sports Bureau did some digging and revealed that Pettitte's numbers through four starts -- a 3-0 record, 1.29 ERA, 22 strikeouts in 28 innings -- are the lowest ERA and also the highest strikeout total that Pettitte has had through his first four games in any of his 16 seasons in the Major Leagues. The veteran lefty will try to keep that rolling against the White Sox, a team he pitched well against last July 30 in Chicago, holding the Pale Hose to an unearned run on five hits in 6 1/3 innings, walking none and fanning eight.
away_pitcher_note: Working on eight days' rest, Garcia posted his second outstanding start in three trips to the mound this season. The right-hander retired 18 of the first 19 Seattle hitters faced and exited after giving up just two runs on two hits over seven innings. Garcia fanned five and walked two during this 103-pitch effort. Garcia will be looking for continued consistency when he pitches in Game 2 of the three-game series at Yankee Stadium going on six days rest. Garcia has a career mark of 4-4 and a 4.21 ERA against the Yankees and is 0-1 in his only start at new Yankee Stadium but was 3-1 at old Yankee Stadium.
summary: 2010-04-30 - Chicago White Sox (4) @ New York Yankees (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez isn't expecting to receive a whole lot of love when he appears in the Bronx on Saturday afternoon, and to be perfectly honest, he hasn't earned much goodwill in 2010. Vazquez struggled again on April 25 against the Angels, allowing five runs in 3 2/3 innings for his third loss in four starts. He no longer believes his issues are purely mechanical and knows patience is running thin with Yankees fans, who still like to pin him as a scapegoat for the 2004 ALCS collapse to the Red Sox. As manager Joe Girardi said, the sooner Vazquez starts winning, the better for everyone involved. He's 3-0 with a 1.88 ERA in three lifetime starts vs. the White Sox, a former club.
away_pitcher_note: Slowly but surely, Danks is becoming the ace of the White Sox staff. Danks worked eight innings against the Mariners on Sunday, marking the second straight start in which he worked eight innings, and picked up his third straight victory when Paul Konerko homered in the eighth inning. Danks gave up just two runs on seven hits, striking out five and not issuing a walk. Over his last three starts, Danks has yielded just 11 hits and four runs in 23 innings, fanning 20 and walking five. He has a 2-1 record and a 6.06 ERA lifetime against the Yankees.
summary: 2010-05-01 - Chicago White Sox (7) @ New York Yankees (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Hughes didn't have great stuff in his last outing, but if that's what it looks like on an off-night, sign him up for more of the same against the White Sox. Hughes held the Orioles to a run on two hits in 5 2/3 innings on April 27 and has made the Yankees look very wise in selecting him over Joba Chamberlain -- and others -- to be their fifth starter. Hughes had a 1.80 ERA in four relief appearances last year against Chicago, spanning five innings, and has made two starts against the White Sox, both in 2008 (no record, 1.50 ERA).
away_pitcher_note: The 4-2 setback suffered by the White Sox ace left-hander Tuesday in Texas marked the 100th loss of his illustrious career, dropping Buehrle to 137-100 overall. Since throwing his perfect game on July 23, 2009, Buehrle has a 4-10 record with a 6.72 ERA. He pitched well enough to win against the Rangers, allowing four runs on seven hits over seven innings. He struck out two, walked one and gave up three of the runs on a home run and double by backup catcher Matt Treanor, who had never faced Buehrle before in his career. Buehrle has a 1-6 career mark against the Yankees with a 6.43 ERA and has made one start with no decision in the new Yankee Stadium.
summary: 2010-05-02 - Chicago White Sox (3) @ New York Yankees (12) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: If you take away the first inning from Peavy's last start, then you would have seen the dominant Peavy everyone expects on the mound for the White Sox. Unfortunately for the right-hander, every inning countS and the five runs allowed in the first inning led to the 6-5 Texas victory and Peavy's fifth straight winless start to begin the season. Peavy had never before opened a season with five straight winless starts. In his last two outings, Peavy has combined for 12 strikeouts and 12 walks, as he tries to implement the changes made in his pitching mechanics put into place two starts ago against Tampa Bay. Peavy has a 3-2 record and a 5.18 ERA over eight starts since joining the White Sox and has a 2-1 career record with a 5.40 ERA against the Royals.
away_pitcher_note: Meche grinded his way through six innings in his last start against the Mariners, giving up five runs on eight hits and three walks. He had command issues, making 115 pitches that included 69 strikes, and was often up in the zone and behind in the count. Both Meche and the ballclub insist that there are no injury problems associated with his stiff shoulder in Spring Training or his aching back of 2009. It's mainly location. Meche is sorting through various remedies but now fears he's tending to tinker too much, trying to make adjustments during the game and creating his own distractions. Maybe he'll find himself against the White Sox, a team that he's handled well in the past. Meche is 8-3 with a 4.00 ERA against them in 17 games and stands 5-2 at U.S. Cellular Field.
summary: 2010-05-03 - Kansas City Royals (1) @ Chicago White Sox (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: A rough month of April came to a close for the right-hander with a victory over the Rangers in Arlington, but Floyd has been a notoriously slow starter throughout his career. He turned in his best 2010 start during Thursday's series finale at Texas, giving up just one earned run on five hits over seven innings, striking out five and not issuing a single walk as the White Sox avoided a three-game sweep. Floyd allowed just one hit over the last three innings of that particular start. His season turnaround might be challenged on Tuesday by the Royals, as he has a 1-5 career record and 4.84 ERA against them. But Floyd also has a 16-9 record and 3.65 ERA lifetime at U.S. Cellular Field.
away_pitcher_note: Not only did Hochevar absorb his first loss last Thursday night at Tampa Bay, his ERA almost doubled. The red-hot Rays savaged him for nine runs on 11 hits and two walks in just 2 2/3 innings. No one seemed to think that Hochevar's stuff was that bad, just that the Rays' hitters were that good. While he'd been neatly avoiding the curse of a big inning, this time, he was nailed with two of them -- for five runs and four runs. The Royals are hoping it's just a one-game blip for Hochevar, who previously showed every indication of fulfilling the promise that made him the nation's top Draft choice in 2006. This will be his sixth start and he did well against the White Sox last year, going 2-0 with a 1.40 ERA in two starts.
summary: 2010-05-04 - Kansas City Royals (7) @ Chicago White Sox (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Garcia struggled mightily in the first inning of his last start against the Yankees, giving up two runs on three hits, before first baseman Paul Konerko started an inning-ending double play to get Garcia out of further trouble. Garcia quickly settled down and retired the next 12 in a row until he gave up Brett Gardner's single and Derek Jeter's game-tying home run. Garcia finished the night with a no-decision, allowing four runs on five hits, while striking out two and walking two. Garcia has not done well against the Royals over the course of his career, posting a dismal 8-13 record with an elevated 6.03 ERA. Garcia was 0-2 against the Royals in 2009.
away_pitcher_note: Bannister performed beautifully last Friday night against Tampa Bay, holding the red-hot Rays to two hits and one run in seven innings of a game the Royals won, 3-2, after he departed. Equally satisfying for Bannister was that his pursuit of becoming a ground-ball pitcher paid off big-time for the first time this year. Thirteen of the 21 outs came on the ground with only three flyouts (never mind that bothersome home run by Evan Longoria). Bannister walked two and got three strikeouts and had his fourth quality start in five outings. Now he runs into the White Sox, against whom he's 3-4 with a 7.61 ERA in 12 games at U.S. Cellular Field, where he's 1-1 but with an 8.14 ERA in five outings.
summary: 2010-05-05 - Kansas City Royals (2) @ Chicago White Sox (9) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander showed his increasing mound confidence and veteran grit by battling through Saturday afternoon's balmy conditions at Yankee Stadium without his best stuff. The left-hander exited after five innings, allowing two runs on six hits over five innings, but elevating his pitch count to a season-high 118 pitches. Danks has limited opponents to two earned runs or fewer in each of his first five starts. According to Elias Sports Bureau, the last White Sox pitcher to accomplish the feat was Jose Contreras, who did so in his first six starts of 2006. Danks gave up one run over seven innings during a victory over the Blue Jays earlier this season at Rogers Centre, and has a career record of 1-2 against Toronto.
away_pitcher_note: Eveland labored through his last start vs. the A's on Saturday, giving up four earned runs on eight hits and three walks over 6 2/3 innings. Really the only significant blemish was a two-run home run to shortstop Cliff Pennington in the fourth. After that, Eveland settled down and cruised through his remaining 2 2/3 innings, before being replaced by lefty Scott Downs. It appears Eveland's 1.93 ERA through his first three starts may have been a facade, but give the big left-hander credit for bouncing back late in his last outing. Against the Indians, Eveland is 2-0 lifetime with a 1.50 ERA in 12 innings.
summary: 2010-05-06 - Toronto Blue Jays (2) @ Chicago White Sox (0) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle's recent struggles continued, as he lost his fourth straight decision overall on Sunday afternoon at Yankee Stadium. The left-hander was victimized by home runs from Brett Gardner and Robinson Cano, both left-handed hitters, and allowed five runs on 10 hits over 4 2/3 innings. He struck out three and walked one, while throwing 93 pitches. Buehrle has given up 18 earned runs on 32 hits over 22 1/3 innings during this four-game skid. While Buehrle slipped to 1-7 lifetime against the Yankees, he brings a 5-3 career record against the Blue Jays into Friday's start and a 78-47 mark at U.S. Cellular Field.
away_pitcher_note: Marcum's run of tough luck ended with his last start, in which he earned his first win since September 11, 2008, against the White Sox. Marcum, who missed last season recovering from Tommy John surgery, went 6 1/3 innings against the A's, allowing a run on six hits and four walks. Marcum fanned six Oakland batters. In his previous five starts in 2010, Marcum had given up more than three runs only one time yet had nothing to show for it in the win column. The last time Marcum faced the Pale Hose, he gave up two runs in 7 1/3 innings on five hits and a walk, striking out six.
summary: 2010-05-07 - Toronto Blue Jays (7) @ Chicago White Sox (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The Peavy who was on the mound during Monday's series-opening victory over the Royals is the Peavy whom the White Sox expect to be  the ace of their staff for this season and beyond. Peavy gave up just four hits over seven scoreless innings, and fanned a season-high nine. Of greater importance was that he only walked one, after issuing 20 free passes during the month of April. Peavy made his only career start against Toronto earlier this season at Rogers Centre and did not factor in the decision after allowing seven runs on eight hits over 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Cecil took a perfect game into the seventh inning in his last start, shutting down the Indians on the first game of the current road trip. Cecil's dominance set the tone in Toronto's 5-1 victory. Jhonny Peralta's RBI single in the seventh inning was the lone hit Cecil allowed in the eight innings he pitched and it scored the Tribe's lone run. Cecil walked two Indians batters and struck out 10. Cecil has faced the White Sox once, beating them on May 5, 2009. Chicago tagged Cecil for three runs on six hits and a pair of walks, and the lefty fanned two.
summary: 2010-05-08 - Toronto Blue Jays (3) @ Chicago White Sox (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The tightrope walked by Gavin Floyd during the first three innings of Tuesday's game against Kansas City finally went out from under him in the seventh inning of a 7-2 loss. The Royals put 10 runners on base against Floyd over those first three frames but scored only two runs. In the seventh, the Royals knocked out four straight hits during a four-run rally that ran the right-hander from the game. Floyd finished with six runs allowed on a career-worst 13 hits. Through 32 2/3 innings, Floyd has yielded 45 hits and issued 14 walks. He has a 0-1 record against the Blue Jays in 2010, having given up four runs on nine hits over six innings in Toronto.
away_pitcher_note: Romero started strong against the Indians in his last outing, fanning five of the first six batters he faced. The lefty had to buckle down for the rest of his six innings, but he picked up his third win of the season, giving up five runs on nine hits and two walks. Romero finished with nine strikeouts against the Tribe but struggled with control, making three wild pitches and pushing his season total to 10. The last time Romero faced the White Sox, he made his signature outing of the young 2010 season, compiling 12 strikeouts and giving up two runs on a hit and two walks over eight innings.
summary: 2010-05-09 - Toronto Blue Jays (9) @ Chicago White Sox (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Slowey helped the Twins complete a sweep of the Tigers on Wednesday, improving his record to 4-2. In the game, Slowey pitched 5 2/3 innings and gave up three runs. All of his earned runs came off solo home runs, but he had the support of the Twins' bats to produce enough hits to hold off the powerful hitting Tigers. Before that game, Slowey hadn't given up more than one home run this season. In total, Slowey gave up seven hits in the game and walked two batters. He also had three strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: As the team's fifth starter, Garcia has been as consistent as any member of the White Sox rotation aside from John Danks. Garcia gave up just two runs on 10 hits over six innings in his last start, against the Royals, to pick up his first victory of the season. The win helped Garcia avoid an 0-3 start for the first time in his career. Garcia fanned four and didn't issue a walk, throwing a mere 84 pitches before giving way to the bullpen. Garcia took the loss in his only start this season against the Twins, but he gave up just two runs on three hits over seven innings. Garcia has a 9-6 career record with a 3.76 ERA against the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Pavano suffered some tough luck in his last start against Baltimore last Thursday. The Twins veteran right-hander pitched eight solid innings and gave up just two runs, while striking out eight Orioles batters. Pavano's lone mistake of the outing was a hanging breaking ball that went for a two-run homer in the 2-0 loss. Pavano yielded six hits and three walks in throwing 97 pitches against Baltimore. Since the Twins had an off-day Monday, Pavano should be well rested pitching on five days' rest when Minnesota welcomes the Chicago White Sox to Target Field.
away_pitcher_note: Danks will hope for a little more run support in his next trip to the hill, as he gave up two runs over seven innings on Thursday against Toronto, only to get the hard-luck loss when the offense was shut out. Six starts into the season, Danks has turned in five quality starts and has not allowed more than two earned runs in any of his six starts. Danks' first start of the campaign was against the Twins, as he went six innings and gave up two runs -- one of them earned. That got him a no-decision. The southpaw is 4-5 lifetime against the Twins with a 5.13 ERA. Even though Danks has started against the Twins more frequently than any other team in his career, this is his first start in the brand-new Target Field.

home_pitcher_note: Meche grinded out eight tough innings in a complete-game, 3-2 loss at Texas last Saturday night. He gave up six hits but his downside was seven walks. All three Rangers runs were scored by batters who walked. Meche issued four of the passes and gave up both runs in the first two innings, then buckled down. Manager Trey Hillman stuck with him in the eighth even though he was heading toward a final 128 pitches, fourth most in his career. Meche faced the White Sox on the last road trip and went just five innings, giving up five runs in a loss.
away_pitcher_note: Buehrle earned a tough-luck no-decision his last time out, giving up three runs over eight innings in a 12-inning loss to the Toronto Blue Jays. He had good command in that outing as he threw 70 of his 101 pitches for strikes, and he set a season high with six strikeouts. Against Kansas City, Buehrle is 20-9 lifetime with a 3.55 ERA over 278 2/3 IP. So far this season, Buehrle has been especially tough on left-handed hitters, allowing them to hit at a 15-for-59 (.254) clip.
summary: 2010-05-14 - Chicago White Sox (1) @ Kansas City Royals (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Getting immersed in the staff tendency toward bases on balls, Hochevar issued four walks and hit a batter, contributing to his exit just 2 2/3 innings into his start last Sunday at Texas. A contributing factor was probably illness because Hochevar was throwing up in the bullpen before the game. The Rangers ousted him in a four-run third inning but he had no decision because the Royals rallied to tie the score. He was coming off a fine performance at Chicago in which he held the White Sox to one unearned run and three hits in six innings. Hochevar earned his third victory, rebounding from a 2 2/3-inning debacle at Tampa Bay in his previous start.
away_pitcher_note: Jake Peavy had electric stuff in his last start against the Blue Jays, as he took a perfect game into the sixth inning before a John Buck home run broke the streak. Peavy fanned eight and walked none in the outing. In his last 15 innings, Peavy has walked one and struck out 17. He last faced the Royals on May 3, and he held them scoreless over seven innings. In four lifetime starts against the Royals, Peavy has a record of 3-1.
summary: 2010-05-15 - Chicago White Sox (5) @ Kansas City Royals (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Bannister set himself up for failure by issuing walks to start each of two innings last Tuesday night against the Indians. Sure enough, both runners scored as he fell behind, 4-1, and was headed for a loss. Bannister gave up an early home run which seemed to make him tentative and he tried to be too fine with his pitches as he put it. He's given up seven home runs, much too fast a pace to suit him especially as he tries to transform himself into a ground-ball pitcher. Bannister faced the White Sox on May 5 at Chicago and lasted just three-plus innings, giving up seven runs on seven hits and four walks. He's faced the White Sox more times than any club in his career, 13, and is 4-4 against them with an 8.22 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Gavin Floyd struggled with wildness in his last start, hitting two batters and giving up five runs in the first three frames. He settled down to go another 3 1/3 innings without giving up a run. His seven strikeouts tied his season high, and he ended up with a no-decision when the White Sox came back to tie the game in the seventh. On the season, Floyd has a 9.00 ERA in the first three innings, compared to a 2.00 ERA in the middle three innings. Against Kansas City in his career, Floyd is 1-6 with a 5.29 ERA. His last start against Kansas City yielded six earned runs in 6 1/3 innings pitched.
summary: 2010-05-16 - Chicago White Sox (3) @ Kansas City Royals (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: After struggling for the better part of a month to find the sinker that induced so many ground-ball outs last year, Porcello put it to work in his last start and got a gem of an outing from it. His seven scoreless innings against the Yankees last Wednesday included 13 groundouts, plus three big swings and misses from his four-seam power fastball. Now he'll try to carry that over against a White Sox team he faced only once last year, giving up five runs over 5 1/3 innings with two homers.
away_pitcher_note: As the fifth starter within the White Sox rotation, Garcia has pitched more like a No. 2 or 3 hurler for most of the 2010 season. The right-hander's latest strong showing came Tuesday night, during the South Siders' debut at Target Field, resulting in a 5-2 victory. Garcia gave up two runs on nine hits over seven innings, striking out three and walking two. Garcia showed his pitching guile by striking out Joe Mauer, the best hitter in Baseball, on three straight split-fingers in the fifth inning to escape a two-on, two-out jam. Garcia has a 16-6 career record against Detroit with a 3.76 ERA and has a 7-3 lifetime mark at Comerica Park.

Danks struck out three, walked three and yielded seven hits over seven innings, including a pair of run-scoring, two-out hits from left-handed hitting Justin Morneau and Denard Span. He threw 109 pitches and 63 for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders is coming off his second career shutout, a four-hit blanking of the A's in a duel with Dallas Braden at Angel Stadium on Friday night. Saunders was in command from the start, pounding the strike zone with fastballs, curves and changeups while walking two and striking out six hitters. He feels he has regained his aggressive mindset after a run of poor starts, trusting his stuff more and getting ahead of hitters. Saunders has excelled in three career starts at U.S. Cellular Field, where he's 2-0 with a 1.66 ERA and 0.83 WHIP. He's 3-2 overall against the White Sox with a 3.49 ERA in six career outings.
summary: 2010-05-19 - Los Angeles Angels (3) @ Chicago White Sox (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: After yielding five runs on four hits in the first inning on April 28 at Texas, Peavy has been dominant. Since then, he has allowed 16 hits and seven runs in 28 2/3 innings, while walking three and striking out 28. Peavy yielded three runs in the first inning in his past outing at Kansas City, but was dominant after that. After surrendering a solo homer to Billy Butler in the third, Peavy gave up only three more hits, all singles. He retired 14 of 15 in one stretch. Peavy has won three straight May starts, after going 0-2 with three no-decisions in his first five starts. He has lowered his 7.85 ERA in April to 5.37.
away_pitcher_note: Santana delivered six solid innings against the Athletics on Saturday, striking out six while yielding three runs (two earned) on seven hits and three walks. He didn't have a crisp fastball early on, but he was getting it up in the 93-94 mph range by the middle innings, and his slider and changeup were effective as well. It was his first win since April 18 when he went the distance in Toronto. Santana is 3-2, 4.88 in nine career games against the White Sox. He's 2-1, 4.79 in four U.S. Cellular Field appearances, three as a starter.
summary: 2010-05-20 - Los Angeles Angels (6) @ Chicago White Sox (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle was extremely sharp in the early going of his last outing at Kansas City. He retired the first 13 hitters and took a 1-0 lead to the sixth. But Buehrle allowed a solo homer to Yuniesky Betancourt in the sixth before the Royals pecked away with a series of bloopers and seeing-eye grounders to post a five-spot in the seventh and send Buehrle to his fifth consecutive loss. Buehrle is determined to stay away from the big inning going forward, but there's not much he can do about it when softly struck balls find holes. For the most part, Buehrle was happy with the pitches he made in Kansas City and hopes to combine the same skill level with a bit of luck in his next start.
away_pitcher_note: "Terrible," is how Nolasco described his last outing. Still, the right-hander collected a victory on a day the Marlins almost blew an early 7-0 lead. In six innings, he gave up three runs (two earned) while striking out three and walking two. Nolasco's velocity was a hair down -- between 88-91 mph. He says it was a bad outing in which he wasn't particularly sharp. For his career, Nolasco if 44-32, which is the fourth-most wins in franchise history.

home_pitcher_note: Floyd took the loss on Sunday in Kansas City, surrendering 10 hits and five earned runs through six innings. Despite those numbers, Floyd felt good about his effort. Several of the hits were grounders that managed to find holes. Floyd didn't allow an extra base hit and thinks the results will come if he makes the pitches that he did against the Royals. Manager Ozzie Guillen said he'd like to see Floyd command his breaking pitches better to set up the fastball. Floyd has gone six innings or more in seven of his eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Not at his best in his last outing, Volstad was victimized by a couple of errors that cost him two earned runs in a loss to Arizona. In five innings, he was tagged for four runs, with two earned. The right-hander had gone at least six innings in six of his first seven starts. On the road this year, Volstad is 1-2 with a 6.17 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia continues to be one of the steadier forces among the White Sox starting rotation, even though he was projected as the franchise's fifth starter entering the season. Garcia shut down the Tigers on Wednesday afternoon at Comerica Park, raising his career ledger to 17-6 against Detroit, after giving up just two runs on five hits over six innings. Garcia will need to live up to his reputation as "Big Game Freddy" with Florida throwing Josh Johnson, one of the National League's top pitchers, in this series finale. Garcia has found great career Interleague success, tied with six others, including Mark Buehrle, for the third-most victories at 19. His 19-7 record is second best to Buehrle in winning percentage and his 2.57 ERA ranks No. 1 in Interleague Play. Garcia has no record against Florida.
away_pitcher_note: Since an Opening Day loss at New York, Johnson is 4-0 with a 2.08 ERA. The right-hander comes off an overpowering performance against the D-backs, striking out nine in seven shutout innings. JJ has fanned 63 in 57 innings this season. He threw 104 pitches against Arizona, which matches his second-most of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Masterson is still looking for his first win since Aug. 20 of last year. He didn't get it against the Royals on Wednesday. He allowed just two runs on five hits, but he needed 106 pitches to get through only five innings of work in a no-decision. He needs to be more efficient, and he needs to improve his performance against left-handers if he's going to have success as a starter. For now, such success has been very elusive to Masterson.
away_pitcher_note: John Danks has pitched well enough to win his last three games, but he has thrice been thwarted by the opposing pitcher pitching just a little bit better than him. In each of his last three starts he's gone seven innings or more and given up three runs or fewer, but he has emerged the hard-luck loser in each contest. In his last start against the Angels, Danks gave up one hit through seven innings. That one hit was a two-run home run to Torii Hunter, and an unearned run in the eighth doomed Danks to the loss. Against the Indians, Danks is 2-5 in 10 career starts, with a 4.89 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Because he has a four-pitch arsenal, Talbot can be fairly effective, even on the days he doesn't have his best stuff. But he didn't have anything to work with in a loss to the Royals on Thursday, and it showed as he allowed six runs on eight hits with three walks and a strikeout over six innings. In general, Talbot has been a pleasant surprise in the back end of the Tribe rotation. But this start was evidence that without overpowering stuff, Talbot will have his rocky days.
away_pitcher_note: Peavy struggled in his last start, giving up six earned runs and earning the loss against the Los Angeles Angels. The six earned runs was the most he had in a start since April 28 against the Rangers. Strangely enough, Peavy piched well in his six innings, fanning eight batters. But a well-executed hit and run and a two-run homer cost Peavy three runs. After the game, Peavy said that he believed he was the reason for the team's 6-5 loss. "It's frustrating for myself, because I feel solely responsible for this loss tonight. Out there, I felt good," he said. Lifetime, he is 1-1 with a 4.70 ERA against the Indians. In his last start against the Indians on April 17, he went 7 1/3 and gave up just two earned runs.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook's streak of two dominant starts ended in his last outing against the Reds, but the veteran righty had only one bad inning against Cincinnati. Victimized by Jonny Gomes' towering two-run shot in the fourth inning, Westbrook gave up three that inning. The Reds ran up his pitch count, and Westbrook checked out after five innings, charged with four runs on seven hits and two walks. Westbrook, who didn't factor into the decision, struck out three. Westbrook had allowed two runs in 15 innings before facing the Reds, winning two straight starts. Westbrook has already faced the White Sox twice this season, losing on Opening Day and taking a no-decision 12 days later. Westbrook has allowed five runs on 10 hits and seven walks in eight innings against the Pale Hose this year, fanning three.
away_pitcher_note: Buehrle returned to form in his last start against the Marlins, as he went eight shutout innings, which was enough to snap what had been a five-game losing streak. Buehrle also stopped what had been a 65-at-bat streak in which he went without a strikeout when he fanned Hanley Ramirez in the sixth inning. The win made Buehrle the third pitcher in baseball history to win 20 games in Interleague Play, along with Mike Mussina and Jamie Moyer. Against the Indians lifetime, he is 12-15, with a 6-7 ledger at Progressive Field.

home_pitcher_note: Niemann picked up his fourth win of the season Saturday night when he held the Astros to two runs on four hits in seven innings. He now has eight quality starts in nine outings; the only outing he did not produce a quality start came in his first start of the season when he got hit by a line drive and had to leave the game after retiring the first four hitters. Because Niemann stands 6-foot-9, he creates a difficult downward angle for hitters, who rarely face a pitcher of his height. He is 1-2 with a 4.67 ERA in three career starts against the White Sox.
away_pitcher_note: Floyd turned in his best start of the season in his last turn, going 6 1/3 innings and giving up just one run, two walks and six hits to go with seven strikeouts. He labored through the first two innings, as it took him 19 and 20 pitches to get through them, but after that he settled down and pitched the next 4 1/3 innings with 58 pitches. In his career, Floyd has won both starts against the Rays, with a 3.21 ERA. Lifetime, he has averaged a strikeout per inning against the Rays, as he has pitched 14 innings and fanned 14 Rays.
summary: 2010-05-27 - Chicago White Sox (1) @ Tampa Bay Rays (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Price overcame first-inning struggles Sunday against the Astros to give the Rays five innings, which allowed the classy left-hander to pick up his seventh win of the season. Price allowed four runs in the first inning and five overall, but showed toughness in the way he battled while fighting his control. The No. 1 pick of the 2007 Draft has shown a lot of improvement in his fastball command, which has made his slider and curve even more effective. He is 0-2 with a 5.73 ERA in two career starts against the White Sox.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia got hit hard in his last outing, as he could not make it out of the third inning against the Marlins. Florida batters went 7-for-14 with two home runs, two walks and two doubles while scoring seven earned runs on Garcia. The three home runs he surrendered in the game marked the most he'd given up in a game since Sept. 23, 2008. Entering the start, Garcia had made three consecutive quality starts. Against the Rays, Garcia is 7-2 with a 3.63 ERA career. Garcia's ERA indoors (4.82) is almost a full run higher than when he is pitching outdoors (3.98).
summary: 2010-05-28 - Chicago White Sox (4) @ Tampa Bay Rays (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Davis will make his 10th start of the season, looking to bounce back from the worst outing by a Rays starter all season -- his 3 2/3 inning performance against the Red Sox on Monday night, when he gave up five earned runs on seven hits, three walks and a home run while failing to strike out anyone. Aside from Jeff Niemann's injury-shortened first start, it was the only time a Tampa Bay starter failed to pitch at least five innings. Davis simply didn't have control of his pitches Monday, as he demonstrated by walking in the second run of the game. The young right-hander looked like a force to be reckoned with following a few strong early season starts, and he will look to get back to that form against the White Sox. Davis had possibly his best start of the year against the White Sox on the road when he went six scoreless innings and gave up just two hits, walked three and struck out six. This will be his second start against Chicago.
away_pitcher_note: Danks got his first win in five starts last time against the Indians, but the lefty didn't have his best stuff. He pitched his way out of jams with runners at second and third with no outs in two separate innings, getting touched up for just two runs on six hits and two walks. But it came at a price. Danks' pitch count soared early, keyed by a 40-pitch fourth inning. He lasted just five innings and struck out five. Danks will look to repeat the success he had against the Rays earlier this season. He made his most dominant start of the season in that game, giving up a run on two hits in eight innings. Danks punched out eight Rays that night.
summary: 2010-05-29 - Chicago White Sox (5) @ Tampa Bay Rays (8) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Shields will make his 11th start of the season looking to build on what was arguably his best outing of the year, a four-hit, five-strikeout performance against the Red Sox on Tuesday. Shields gave up two runs on one hit in the third inning but responded by retiring 16 straight batters from the third inning until he left the game after eight. The right-hander has been great in May, posting a 2.65 ERA in his five starts this month and going at least eight innings in three of them. He leads the American League with 69 1/3 innings and is second in strikeouts, having fanned 71 batters -- a high number for someone who says he doesn't focus on striking out batters. This will be Shields' second start of the year against the White Sox. He gave up just two runs in seven innings against them on April 22, allowing six hits and three walks while striking out three. In six career starts against Chicago, Shields is 2-1 with a 4.17 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander gave the White Sox world a bit of a scare following his last start at Progressive Field when talking about how he just didn't feel good on the mound. But as Peavy said two days later, it was just much to do about nothing. His 7-3 loss to Cleveland, during which Peavy allowed six runs on eight hits over six innings, was just one of those starts among 33 or 34 where he didn't have his best stuff. Peavy would like to close out this road trip on a high note, as well as finish off a rough two-month stretch to begin the 2010 campaign, when he faces the Rays at Tropicana Field. Peavy sits two wins away from 100 for his career and has a 1-1 career mark against Tampa Bay.
summary: 2010-05-30 - Chicago White Sox (8) @ Tampa Bay Rays (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Wednesday's afternoon of work was so abbreviated for Buehrle that he volunteered to pitch out of the bullpen on Friday night in St. Petersburg, which would have been his side day to throw.
