Buehrle enters the contest with Texas carrying a 4.38 ERA overall in 10 starts. He has an 0-1 mark against Texas this year, but has an 11-4 lifetime ledger, including a no-hitter thrown against the Rangers at U.S. Cellular Field in 2007.
away_pitcher_note: Harden allowed six runs, five earned, in 51/3 innings against the Royals on Tuesday. He walked two, struck out five and did not get a decision in the Rangers 8-7 victory. The Rangers have won three of his last four starts although he did not get a decision. He has a 7.85 ERA and opponents are hitting .313 off him in those four starts. Because of the off-days, Harden will be pitching on six days' rest. He is 10-5 with a 2.66 ERA in 28 career starts when starting on six or more days of rest. He is 4-3 with a 3.19 ERA in eight starts against the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: The months of April and May mercifully have come to an end for Floyd, who bounced back from a similar slow start in 2009 to post a 3-0 record and 1.28 ERA in June. Floyd posted a 6.49 ERA in April this season and followed up that lofty number with a 5.63 ERA in May. Floyd is coming off a loss to the Rays during which he gave up three runs on four hits over seven innings, striking out five and walking one, in making his second straight quality start. One of Floyd's two wins this year has come against Texas, while he has a lifetime mark of 1-1 against the Rangers.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman, after losing 5-2 to the Royals on Wednesday, is now 1-3 with a 6.97 ERA in his last five starts. He is 0-4 with a 7.71 ERA in four starts on the road after winning a club record 12 games on the road last season. Left-handers are hitting .319 off him while right-handers are batting .294. He made one start against the White Sox earlier this year and allowed three runs, one earned, in six innings. He allowed just two hits and walked four. He is 1-1 with a 3.83 ERA in three starts and five relief appearances against the White Sox in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia showed the importance of a veteran presence on the mound during the White Sox 4-2 victory over the Rays on Friday night. After getting crushed by the Marlins during his last start at home on Sunday, Garcia came back to absolutely shut down the best team in baseball by record. The right-hander gave up just two runs on four hits over seven innings, setting a season high with seven strikeouts and walking two. Garcia needed a mere 89 pitches to get through the seven frames at Tropicana Field. Garcia has not faced Texas this season, but has a 6-5 career mark against the Rangers. Garcia also has a 3-1 record on the road in 2010 but just a 1-2 mark at home, with a slightly lower 5.24 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Lewis was 1-3 with a 4.11 ERA in May. He lost to the Twins, 2-1, on Friday by allowing two runs in six innings. He struck out just one and walked four. It's the fourth time this season he has walked four or more in a game. He is 1-3 with a 3.65 ERA in six starts on the road. Opponents are hitting .204 off him, but he has walked 28 while striking out 59 in 63 1/3 innings. He struck out a season-low one against the Twins on Friday. Opponents are hitting .154 off him with runners in scoring position.

home_pitcher_note: Saturday's 8-5 loss to the Rays marked the lone blemish on an otherwise All-Star-caliber season for the young left-hander. Danks had not allowed more than three runs in a start during his first nine trips to the mound, but was pounded for eight runs on eight hits over four-plus innings at Tropicana Field. It was Danks' first loss at the Rays' home. He struck out two and walked three, but Danks threw 102 pitches. Danks has a 1-0 record against the Indians this season and has a 3-5 career mark. Danks enters the start with a 35-37 career record and has a lifetime mark of 15-21 at U.S. Cellular Field.
away_pitcher_note: With plenty of speculation about his fate in the Indians' rotation, Masterson turned in one of his strongest starts as a member of the Tribe on Sunday in the Bronx. He went 6 2/3 innings against a dangerous lineup and allowed three runs on seven hits, striking out eight. But he was a victim of more tough luck, as the bullpen let him down and he was saddled with a no-decision. So Masterson's stretch of 11 consecutive losing decisions remains intact. He hasn't notched a win since last Aug. 20. He's still on somewhat shaky ground, but he improved his standing with this strong start.

home_pitcher_note: When Peavy takes the mound on Saturday night against the Indians at U.S. Cellular Field, the right-hander will be in search of his 100th career victory. Peavy hopes to hit that target with a bit more ease than it took to pick up No. 99 on Sunday in St. Petersburg. Peavy allowed five runs on 10 hits over 5 1/3 innings, striking out five, and exiting in the sixth at 110 pitches. Peavy has given up 17 earned runs over 17 1/3 innings in his past three starts and needed 34 pitches to get through a two-run fifth inning alone against the Rays. Peavy has a 0-1 record against Cleveland this year and a 1-2 mark lifetime against the Indians. He holds a 4-2 record at U.S. Cellular.
away_pitcher_note: Talbot turned in a gritty start against the Yankees on Monday, giving the Tribe 6 1/3 respectable innings against a tough lineup. He was not rewarded for his efforts, as his supporting cast in the bullpen and the lineup let him down. Talbot was charged with three runs on nine hits with no walks and three strikeouts, and he was handed a fourth loss that he arguably didn't deserve. Talbot pitched his way out of several jams, which ran up his pitch count. He hopes to have a little more luck against the Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle struggled through his last start, a 5 1/3-inning effort against the Rangers. After Buehrle threw 34 pitches in the first inning, yet danced out of trouble, the Rangers finally got to him to the tune of five runs in the sixth inning. Buehrle managed to not allow a run through the first two innings, despite allowing four hitters to reach base. In that sixth inning, four consecutive hitters singled, and Buehrle left the game tied at 4. Buehrle walked only one but allowed 12 hits, including 10 singles. In his career, Buehrle is 12-15 in 39 starts against the Indians.
away_pitcher_note: If Westbrook wasn't all the way back to his pre-injury form before Tuesday night's start at Comerica Park, he might be now. Westbrook was magnificent in guiding the Tribe to a 3-2 victory over the Tigers on Tuesday. He worked quickly, stayed ahead and allowed just one run on five hits with a walk and a strikeout over 7 2/3 innings. In April, Westbrook returned from a 22-month absence following Tommy John surgery. His rust showed early in the season, but his command has improved as the year has rolled along. And in this game, he was at his best, no doubt fueling speculation that he might be targeted by contenting clubs at next month's Trade Deadline.

home_pitcher_note: Floyd had pitched well going into his last start, against the Texas Rangers, but 2 2/3 innings later, he had been chased after allowing eight hits and six runs after just 19 batters. Of the eight hits he surrendered, five were extra-base hits, including four doubles. After the game, White Sox skipper Ozzie Guillen said, "Maybe the first year in his career here, but I don't think I've ever seen him this bad. Bouncing balls, getting hit hard. That's the first time I've seen him pitching this way. This kid, every time he is in there, we believe we have a chance. Nothing was working with him. I tried to stay with him as long as I can, because our bullpen is very thin, and I couldn't." Floyd is undefeated against the Tigers, with five wins over no losses, and a 3.34 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Hard to believe now, but there had been speculation that Galarraga would be skipped in the Tigers' rotation here with the team off on Monday. Of course, that speculation was before Galarraga's would-be perfect game last Wednesday, when only an errant call from first-base umpire Jim Joyce kept Galarraga from becoming the first Tiger ever to achieve perfection. Tuesday will mark Galarraga's first start since that amazing outing and the incredible sympathy he showed afterwards towards Joyce. He might never pitch anywhere near that well again, but if he can find that same nasty sinker and slider, he'll have a chance to pitch effectively and give the Tigers a chance at a victory.

home_pitcher_note: Even though Garcia entered the season as the nominal fifth starter for the White Sox, he's pitched like their ace so far. Not only do his five wins pace the team, but his 4.94 ERA is the second-lowest of the five starters. In his last start, Garcia went seven innings, giving up three runs. The White Sox offense bailed him out, however, by scoring four runs in those seven innings, earning Garcia the win. Lifetime against the Tigers, Garcia is 17-6 with a 3.73 ERA in 185 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Porcello will look to even his record as he faces the White Sox in game two of a three-game series Wednesday. In his last start, Porcello was shaky in a no-decision against the Indians last Thursday, allowing six runs -- three earned -- on seven hits, while striking out two in 5 1/3 innings. Before his mishap against the Indians, Porcello had made four-straight solid starts and he will look to get back on track in Chicago. Porcello has never pitched at U.S. Cellular field, but is 0-2 with a 6.57 ERA against the White Sox in two career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Danks struggled in his last start en route to earning a loss against the undermanned Cleveland Indians. Danks cruised through his first five innings, but he could not keep it going, eventually letting five of six Indians batters reach base in the sixth. Danks earned the loss on four earned runs in 5 1/3 innings. Jhonny Peralta's double provided the biggest blow to Danks' sixth. Lifetime against the Tigers, Danks is 2-3 with a 4.10 ERA in eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off his fifth loss of the season, Scherzer is looking to rebound from a shaky performance in Kansas City. Scherzer lasted just five-plus innings, allowing five earned runs on nine hits. Detroit manager Jim Leyland said that Scherzer would never become a complete pitcher until he perfects his slider -- something Scherzer is hoping to work on against Chicago. This is Scherzer's first career start against the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Wells' string of first-inning nightmares continued on Sunday in his start at Houston. The Astros rattled off five hits in a row, including a two-run homer by Carlos Lee, in the first inning en route to a 6-3 victory over the Cubs. It continued a disturbing trend for Wells; on May 6, the Pirates batted around against the right-hander, scoring five runs in the first. He lasted two innings in that start. On May 28, the Cardinals smacked six consecutive hits off Wells, who failed to retire a batter. He was pulled after 16 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Peavy's last start was a lost duel against rookie Mitch Talbot. Despite going seven innings and only giving up two earned runs, Talbot gave up one fewer, and earned the win as the Indians held onto the win. Peavy struck out three while only giving up six hits. This is Peavy's first appearance against the Cubs, who nearly acquired him in a trade during the 2008 offseason before eventually being dealt the crosstown White Sox during the '09 season.

home_pitcher_note: Silva tossed seven innings in his last start in Pittsburgh on Monday, surrendering one run on four hits and got the win. He made history, becoming the first Cubs starter since Ken Holtzman, who went 9-0 in 1967, to open a season with eight wins and no losses. Silva joined some pretty special company, considering the last pitcher in the Major Leagues to do that with any team was CC Sabathia, who went 8-0 in his first 10 starts with the Brewers in 2008. He also became the first Cubs starter to begin his Cubs career 8-0 in 100 years. King Cole started 8-0 back in 1910.
away_pitcher_note: Buerhle only netted three innings and gave up six runs in his last start, but he was taken off the hook when his counterpart, Jake Westbrook, also gave up six runs and allowed Buehrle to sneak by with a no-decision despite his poor outing. Buehrle threw 95 pitches despite only going those three innings. Buehrle's outing was over as soon as Lou Marson, who had not homered before in the season, took Buehrle deep with two runners on base to bring his earned run total to six runs. Lifetime against the crosstown rival Cubs, Buehrle is 4-4 with a 4.58 ERA in 11 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly did not get a decision in his last start against the Brewers. It was his sixth straight quality start -- and he has not earned a win in any of them. According to Elias Sports Bureau, Lilly is the second pitcher in Cubs history to go winless over six consecutive quality starts. The other was Sheriff Blake in 1926. Lilly struck out six Brewers, a season high, and gave up one run on Corey Hart's home run. Maybe this time, he'll get some run support.
away_pitcher_note: Floyd pitched well enough to win his last start, as he held Detroit to one run in six innings. He left the bases loaded in the second inning, and followed that up by leaving two on in the third. The only run was scored when Brandon Inge's single in the sixth knocked in Ryan Raburn, who led off the frame with a double. Unfortunately for Floyd, he didn't get the win, as the bullpen imploded in the seventh inning and the Tigers pushed across six runs. Floyd has one career start against the Cubs, and in that start he went seven innings, giving up one run over four hits.

home_pitcher_note: Lincoln will make his home debut in this game, as the Pirates open up the home portion of their Interleague schedule. The former first-round pick made his Major League debut on Wednesday and allowed five earned runs on seven hits and two walks in six innings. Though his line didn't stand out, the performance was largely viewed as a success. Lincoln effectively used his changeup, which was a pitch he really focused on developing in Triple-A earlier this season. With what Lincoln has done in the Minors over the past two years, he's given the Pirates no reason not to believe that he won't make the rotation better.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia continued his run of quality starts, notching his seventh in eight tries, this time against the Detroit Tigers. He went seven innings and gave up solo home runs to Brennan Boesch and Miguel Cabrera. Of his seven quality starts, two have come against the Tigers, and the rest have come against the likes of the Rays, Yankees, Twins and Rangers. Garcia danced in and out of trouble in the game, allowing two hits in three different innings, but only allowing three runs on the evening. Lifetime against the Pirates, Garcia is 2-0 with 12 innings in two starts.

home_pitcher_note: After being the team's most consistent starter during the first half of 2009, Duke cannot seem to find that key to consistency this year. Duke has won just once in his last 11 games and has been pegged with the loss in each of his last three starts. His problems largely stem from one bad inning, and Duke has yet to be able to rely on his best pitch -- the sinker -- to get him out of jams consistently. The good news is that Duke does seem to have a string of good innings (even dominance) in most of his starts. Now, if he can keep from hitting a wall in the middle innings, he'd be on the right track. Duke is 0-1 with a 4.95 ERA in three career starts against the White Sox.
away_pitcher_note: John Danks pitched extremely well in his last start, allowing only a single hit to the Detroit Tigers en rout to earning his fifth victory of the season. The southpaw rebounded from a disastrous past two starts, in which he gave up 12 earned runs in just 9 1/3 innings. Danks did not allow a runner into scoring position in the entirety of his seven innings pitched. He also fanned four and walked four. Danks has not started a game against the Pirates in his career, but in all Interleague games, he is 3-2 with a 2.58 ERA in 10 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Though Ohlendorf gave up six runs in six innings his last time out, there were some positives to be cited afterward. The velocity on the right-hander's fastball and slider were both up. He also had a pretty effective sinker working for him most of the night. That was the good news. On the other end, Ohlendorf remains winless in eight season starts and struggled to close innings out in his last start. All six runs scored against him came with two down, and it was mostly a result of leaving pitches up. Ohlendorf still hasn't found the type of groove he did late last season. He is 0-1 with a 7.45 ERA in two career appearances (one start) against the White Sox.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander bounced back from consecutive rough starts against Texas and Cleveland at U.S. Cellular Field by shutting out the Cubs over 6 2/3 innings during Saturday's 2-1 victory at Wrigley Field. Buehrle struck out a season-high seven, his biggest total since Sept. 5, 2008 against the Angels, and didn't issue a walk. He also allowed no earned runs for the fourth time this season, after accomplishing the same feat just five times in 2009. Buehrle is tied with Mike Mussina for the all-time Interleague victory lead at 21.

home_pitcher_note: It's safe to call Strasburg the stopper. He helped the Nationals end a modest two-game losing skid and defeat the Indians, 9-4, in front of 32,976 at Progressive Field on Sunday afternoon. It was Strasburg's second Major League start, and he picked up right where he left off in his debut before faltering in the sixth inning.  Strasburg struck out eight batters while allowing just two hits, including a solo home run by Travis Hafner, but he walked five of the last 12 batters he faced -- several while experiencing issues with the mound -- and exited with the bases loaded and a 6-1 lead in the bottom of the sixth inning.
away_pitcher_note: Floyd's gem was overshadowed and went for naught Sunday. Pitching in front of a national television audience and going head-to-head with the crosstown rival Cubs, Floyd tossed 6 2/3 innings before allowing a hit. He went the distance, giving up just one run on three hits while walking three and striking out nine in a 1-0 loss. Counterpart Ted Lilly and closer Carlos Marmol one-hit the White Sox to doom Floyd, who has not won a decision since May 22 against the Marlins. Sunday marked the third time Floyd had carried a no-hitter that late in the game, having lost the bids within a one-month span in 2008 against the Tigers and Twins in the eighth and ninth innings, respectively. In four career appearances (two starts) against the Nationals, Floyd is 1-1 with a 4.74 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Right-hander J.D. Martin pitched 7 2/3 innings against the Indians, but he gave up seven runs, six of which were earned. Carlos Santana highlighted a four-run inning by hitting a two-run double. In the fifth inning, he hit a solo home run.
away_pitcher_note: Right arm soreness moved back Peavy to Saturday after he was scheduled to go Thursday against the Pirates. But an MRI revealed no structural damage for the right-hander, who will make his first start in eight days. His last outing, against the Cubs, earned him career win No. 100. He gave up just two runs on six hits in seven innings while striking out five, getting back to .500 in the process. In nine career starts against the Nationals, Peavy is 2-4 with a 4.18 ERA. He has never pitched in Nationals Park, despite spending the majority of 2008 and 2009 with the Padres in the National League.

home_pitcher_note: In Lannan's last start, he was hit hard in a 7-4 loss to Detroit on June 15.  Against the Tigers, he gave up seven runs -- six earned -- on 10 hits in 4 1/3 innings. In the bottom of the fourth inning, Magglio Ordonez' RBI double to left-center field ended Lannan's outing. In his last three games, Lannan has given up 28 hits and 17 runs to earn two losses and a no-decision.  He has never faced the White Sox.
away_pitcher_note: After Garcia's last start, manager Ozzie Guillen said he was the one thing his team felt good about. Garcia failed to make it through seven innings for the first time in his last four starts Tuesday, but it was still enough to get the win at PNC Park. The right-hander went 5 2/3 innings against the Pirates, giving up four runs on eight hits while walking two and striking out one. The 35-year-old has won his last four starts and seven of his last eight after starting the season with two consecutive losses. Garcia is 4-1 with a 5.45 ERA in six road starts this season. He has never faced the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: Danks will look to continue his recent success, as he has won his past two starts. In his most recent outing, a 7-2 victory against Pittsburgh, Danks allowed two runs on four hits in eight innings.  It was his ninth quality start of the season. Danks has never faced Atlanta in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Since allowing a career-high eight earned runs in 1 2/3 innings against the Reds on May 20, Hanson has gone 4-0 with a 2.03 ERA. The tall right-hander had little trouble while scattering three hits over seven scoreless innings against the Rays on Wednesday. He is 4-0 with a 0.75 ERA in four career Interleague starts, producing scoreless efforts against the Yankees, Red Sox and Rays over that span. In his seven road starts this season, Hanson has gone 4-1 with a 2.34 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: In Buehrle's most recent start, he pitched strong in the White Sox's 5-4 win against Pittsburgh.  Buehrle allowed two runs on six hits with six strikeouts in 7 1/3 innings.  He left the game in the eighth inning with his team leading 5-1, and though three Pirates runs off three pitchers brought Pittsburgh within a run, the White Sox held on to deliver Buehrle the win.  Buehrle is 1-0 against Atlanta with a 3.38 ERA.  In his one matchup against the Braves, he gave up three runs on eight hits in eight innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson has seemingly regained the dominant form that he possessed for the A's during the early years of this century. The 34-year-old right-hander, who missed most of the 2009 season while recovering from Tommy John surgery, has allowed three earned runs or less in each of his past 14 starts. In his past 10 outings, Hudson has gone 6-1 with a 2.00 ERA and limited opponents to a .216 batting average. He is 3-2 with a 5.19 ERA in seven career starts against the White Sox. But in his three career starts at U.S. Cellular Field, he is 0-2 with a 13.17 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Floyd is coming off one of his best starts of the season, a 2-1 White Sox victory against the Nationals on June 18.  In that game, Floyd allowed one run on four hits in eight innings.  He also had five strikeouts and one walk.  Alex Rios' RBI single in the 11th inning propelled the White Sox to a win.  In four career games against Atlanta, he is 1-1 with a 9.95 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Other than allowing two seven-run efforts in his past nine outings, the veteran sinkerballer has been fantastic on the mound. In his other seven starts during that stretch, Lowe has allowed three earned runs or fewer in each. During his last two outings, the 37-year-old has completed six innings in each while allowing just five earned runs total. Though his strikeout totals have never been extremely high, Lowe continues to have good control, walking nine batters in his past five starts combined. The right-hander leads the Braves in wins on the year.

home_pitcher_note: Peavy is set to take on the Cubs again. In his last outing against the Nationals, he was the Peavy who won the 2007 NL Cy Young Award, pitching a shutout. More impressively, he yielded just three hits and two walks for the duration of the game. Before the game, such an output would have been unexpected, considering he had a fluid buildup in his right shoulder. On Tuesday, Peavy said, "There's not tears or any significant injuries in there that you can make worse by pitching. That was the biggest thing with me, knowing we're structurally sound. Certainly I want to get out there and I want to be healthy enough to throw bullpens in between, really throw a baseball to work on things and not have to take the mound like we have the last couple times." Two starts ago, Peavy took on the Cubs, going seven innings and giving up two runs in a 10-5 White Sox win.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano did not face the White Sox in the team's first Interleague series at Wrigley Field. The right-hander is coming off his best outing since returning to the rotation June 4. Against the Angels, he gave up one run on eight hits over seven innings and struck out seven. The seven innings were a season high, and he picked up his first win at Wrigley since July 12, 2009. The right-hander will miss hitting at the American League ballpark. He had two singles and drove in a run in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia got another win in his last start, going seven innings and allowing three runs against the Nationals. Washington scored all three runs in a big third inning. In the frame, Cristian Guzman led off the inning with a triple, followed by Adam Dunn's RBI fielder's choice. After the game, Dunn admitted it was hard to pick up the ball out of Garcia's hand. "He had a lot of movement on all of his pitches," Dunn said. "He is really deceptive being a big guy. He hides the ball very well. He was tough to pick up. He was just tough today." Lifetime against the Cubs, Garcia is 4-0 in five starts with an anemic 1.25 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Silva was supposed to start Thursday against his former team, the Mariners, but the right hamstring tweak that got him pulled from his last start after 69 pitches forced the Cubs to juggle the rotation, so now Silva will pitch against the White Sox. Silva is coming off his second straight loss, but it was his team-leading 10th quality start. He won his first eight decisions with the Cubs and has dropped two in a row, although he has pitched well enough to win both. If he goes deep, he's tough. Silva has a 2.07 ERA when he throws at least six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Danks struggled early in his last start against the Braves, but he settled down quite nicely, at one point getting 10 consecutive batters out en route to putting up his third consecutive win. He did not allow another run, and only two singles after those rough first two innings. "My job tonight was to keep it at three," Danks said. "It was fortunate that these guys gave us nine. It made it a little bit easier on us." Lifetime against the Cubs, Danks is 2-0 in three starts, with a sparkling 0.90 ERA over those 20 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster is coming off a tough loss. He gave up two runs on five hits, including a homer, over eight innings, yet took the loss in a 2-0 defeat to Seattle. With the loss, Dempster is 2-1 with a 3.08 ERA in four starts this month. Dempster did not face the White Sox when the two teams met at Wrigley Field.

home_pitcher_note: Lerew is standing in for Luke Hochevar, put on the DL with a stiff right elbow. In his second start, last Tuesday at Washington, he did well enough for 5 1/3 innings, considering there was a rain delay, giving up four runs and keeping the Royals in the game, which they lost.
away_pitcher_note: Buehrle danced in and out of trouble in his last spot, when he earned a win against the Braves last Wednesday. Over the course of his six innings, the Braves left some seven runners on base, including the bases loaded in the sixth. His most impressive Houdini act came in the fifth, however, when he struck out Martin Prado and Jason Heyward back-to-back with runners on first and third to end the inning. Buehrle improved his record to 6-6 on the season and stretched his personal win streak to three games. In his last start against the Royals, Buehrle went six innings and gave up five earned runs in a losing effort. Lifetime, he is 20-10 with 289 hits in 284 2/3 innings.
summary: 2010-06-28 - Chicago White Sox (1) @ Kansas City Royals (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Bannister got back on track last Wednesday after two poor outings, and he couldn't have been much better. He worked six scoreless innings against the Nationals, allowing five hits and two walks.
away_pitcher_note: Gavin Floyd has pitched superbly in his last three starts, but emerges from those starts with an 0-1 record. In those starts, Ted Lilly took a no-hitter into the ninth, Stephen Strasburg held the White Sox to one run and Derek Lowe took a shutout into the seventh.
summary: 2010-06-29 - Chicago White Sox (4) @ Kansas City Royals (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: After a dreary post-Cy Young getaway, Greinke is 2-0 with a no-decision in his past three starts. His fastball is hotter, his slider crisper and his command is sharper.
away_pitcher_note: Jake Peavy shut down the Cubs for the second time in three starts on Friday, managing to hold the North Siders scoreless through seven innings of work. Peavy left the start having thrown 21 consecutive scoreless innings, two short of his career high.
summary: 2010-06-30 - Chicago White Sox (6) @ Kansas City Royals (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Hoping to give Lewis as much rest as possible, the Rangers pushed him back from Wednesday to Friday. He had a three-game win streak snapped in a 7-4 loss to the Astros on Friday, allowing a season-high nine hits. Opponents were 4-for-8 with RISP.
away_pitcher_note: Freddy Garcia continued to be the improbable ace of the White Sox, collecting his ninth win of the season in holding the Cubs to just two runs despite giving up eight hits. Garcia's nine wins are most on the staff, ahead of Jake Peavy's seven.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Hunter allowed one run on five hits with a strikeout in six innings. He's held opponents to two earned runs or fewer in all five starts this season and has registered quality starts in four of those. His only non-quality start was cut short due to injury.
away_pitcher_note: John Danks presided over the Sox first loss in some 11 games in his last start, a 8-6 defeat to the Cubs. After the game, Danks said, "I flat-out stunk; there's no other way to put it. You have to credit them for hitting my mistakes."

home_pitcher_note: Feldman kept the Rangers in the game against the Angels on Tuesday, exiting with a 3-all tie and two runners on, but both runners later scored on a three-run double by Bobby Abreu. As a result, Feldman allowed five runs on nine hits over 5 2/3 innings and took the loss.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Buehrle struggled with his control as he walked five of the 30 batters he faced en route to his sixth loss of the season. In previous three starts, he had only walked two of the 81 batters he faced. Buehrle will look to climb back to .500.

home_pitcher_note: Floyd picked up his third win of the season in his last start against the Royals when he lasted 6 2/3 innings, allowing three runs (two earned) on seven hits with no walks and two strikeouts. Over his last five starts, Floyd has an ERA of 1.28.
away_pitcher_note: Kazmir continues to have trouble getting deep in games with his inability to put hitters away. He has not found his slider to support his low-90s fastball and changeup. He is averaging 5.4 innings per outing, putting a strain on the bullpen.
summary: 2010-07-05 - Los Angeles Angels (2) @ Chicago White Sox (9) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Coming into his last start, Peavy was riding a 21-inning scoreless streak as he squared off against the Royals. The streak ended with a home run in the first, and the White Sox lost, 7-6. Peavy went six innings, allowing three earned runs on seven hits in his sixth loss.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver's dominance has peaked over his last three starts, surrendering a total of nine hits and two earned runs in 21 innings while striking out 28 hitters and walking three. With four quality pitches, he is a likely All-Star after missing out last season.
summary: 2010-07-06 - Los Angeles Angels (1) @ Chicago White Sox (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: In Garcia's last start, he gave up three runs to the Texas Rangers in a no-decision. Garcia kept his five-game personal winning streak intact as he has always seemed to come to play against the best teams in baseball.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders has put together two consecutive outstanding starts after two outings he'd rather forget. Saunders has been a much more effective pitcher on the road, where his ERA is 3.35 in seven starts. That's more than two runs fewer than he's allowed at home.
summary: 2010-07-07 - Los Angeles Angels (2) @ Chicago White Sox (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Danks had his second consecutive subpar outing and consequently earned his second consecutive loss. Even though his six innings and two earned runs were not bad, they were outshone by Tommy Hunter of the Rangers, who held the White Sox to a single run.
away_pitcher_note: Santana had the misfortune of a cold lineup behind him and an opposing pitcher who threw six perfect innings against him in his last start against the Royals, but through seven he had allowed just two hits. Santana has gone 11 straight starts with a decision.
summary: 2010-07-08 - Los Angeles Angels (0) @ Chicago White Sox (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle got back to .500 in his last start, winning for the fourth time in five starts, this time over the Texas Rangers. The start was a seven-inning, three-run performance. It was good enough to get the win on the strength of a three-run sixth by the offense.
away_pitcher_note: Continuing a remarkable comeback, Chen went six perfect innings in a 4-2 victory over the Angels last Saturday night. In 7 1/3 innings, he used just 94 pitches and his only walk was intentional. Chen is 4-2 in seven starts since taking Gil Meche's spot in the rotation.
summary: 2010-07-09 - Kansas City Royals (2) @ Chicago White Sox (8) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: In Floyd's last start, he gave the Los Angeles Angels fits, pitching seven innings of one-run baseball. He has been dynamic of late, holding opposing offenses to one run per start over his last six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Bannister wasn't at his best Monday at Seattle but he kept the Royals in the game and they won in the 10th inning. He went seven innings, giving up four runs on six hits and two walks while using 111 pitches. This will be his fourth shot at the White Sox this year; he's 1-2.
summary: 2010-07-10 - Kansas City Royals (1) @ Chicago White Sox (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Hudson was recalled by the White Sox from Charlotte to replace the injured Jake Peavy in Sunday's series finale with the Royals, as Peavy will have season-ending shoulder surgery. Last season, Hudson made six appearances for the White Sox -- including two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Anthony Lerew, skipped over in the last turn of the rotation, stepped in to make Sunday's start against the White Sox, because Royals ace Zack Greinke was scratched due to discomfort in the back of his right shoulder.
summary: 2010-07-11 - Kansas City Royals (5) @ Chicago White Sox (15) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Slowey has been scuffling of late, like many of the Twins starters. But he threw two perfect innings in relief during the club's last series before the All-Star break on his usual side session day.
away_pitcher_note: Danks briefly flirted with history in his last start, holding the Angels hitless for six innings until Reggie Willits lined a single up the middle for the Angels' first hit of the ballgame. It didn't matter, however, as Danks pitched a shutout to win 1-0.

home_pitcher_note: One problem for Liriano of late has been his inability to keep himself calm in the early innings of big games. The lefty has been overthrowing in those situations, which has resulted in him putting his team in a hole.
away_pitcher_note: Floyd held the Royals scoreless through his first seven innings, but in the eighth the Royals pushed across a run to get on the scoreboard. By that time, the White Sox had already scored five runs and the game was well in hand.

home_pitcher_note: His teammates have called Pavano the club's stopper and he certainly has been their most consistent starter. Pavano is 5-0 in his last seven starts and has been a steadying force in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Buehrle pitched a game that had his former teammate and current Royals leadoff hitter Scott Podsednik calling a "vintage Buehrle" performance. He danced in and out of trouble, at one point stranding four runners on base in two innings to earn the win.

home_pitcher_note: Twins manager Ron Gardenhire has decided to keep Blackburn in the rotation for now, but he has to pitch better to remain there. Too many fastballs and sliders in Blackburn's last start vs. the Tigers resulted in trouble.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia earned his team-high ninth win in his last start, holding the Angels at bay for six innings, giving up five hits and two walks. Garcia has made a habit of earning wins against the teams at the top of the standings, as he has pitched his best in those games.

home_pitcher_note: Pauley makes his second start of the season and the first one was a good one. He limited the Yankees to two hits and one earned run over five innings, but he absorbed the loss. He's a pitch-to-contact hurler and must keep the ball down to be successful.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie right-hander is trying to secure a rotation spot as Jake Peavy's injury replacement. Hudson didn't earn the win in his only other 2010 start against the Royals, despite the White Sox scoring 15 runs, as he was pulled after four-plus innings and five runs allowed.

home_pitcher_note: One bad inning got the second half off to a rocky start, though Fister said he felt good and strong in his 5 2/3-inning stint against the Angels. But his command still isn't as sharp as it was earlier in the season and he surrendered a season-high 12 hits.
away_pitcher_note: Double-digit victories for a third straight season are on the line for Danks after rattling off two straight wins. Danks also has the chance to go over .500 for his career, currently sitting at 40-40.

home_pitcher_note: Lack of run support continues to haunt the staff ace, who is coming off his career-high fifth complete game of the season, albeit a one-run loss to the Angels. His trademark two-seam fastball took the night off, but he found a way to hold the hitters at bay.
away_pitcher_note: Four errors committed by the usually sure-handed White Sox defense led to three unearned runs and a tough loss for Floyd Friday in Minneapolis. Floyd has not performed well in Seattle, with a 1-4 mark and 7.41 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill gave up five earned runs Saturday -- all coming in the second inning -- as he lasted 6 2/3 innings with four walks and three strikeouts. To Cahill's credit, after that inning, he retired the next 16 straight batters as the A's won, 6-5.
away_pitcher_note: No team has handled the White Sox ace like Oakland, during the length of his stellar decade-long career. The A's have a 12-3 mark against Buehrle, who has worked seven innings in each of his past three starts, and are 6-0 in Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Mazzaro threw a career-high 7 2/3 innings in his last start against Kansas City as he picked up his fifth win of the season in a 9-6 victory, which completed a series sweep of the Royals. He allowed only one run with a walk and five strikeouts on the day.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia should have recorded his 10th victory overall in Minnesota, if not for Bobby Jenks' blown save and the Twins' four-run rally in the ninth. Garcia has a 7-1 record after White Sox losses and has made 13 quality starts out of 17.

home_pitcher_note: Braden finished 4 2/3 innings on Tuesday against the Red Sox, allowing four runs (one earned) on 10 hits, in his first start since returning from the 15-day DL with elbow stiffness. Braden is the first pitcher to go winless in nine starts after throwing a perfect game.
away_pitcher_note: Did Hudson's stellar effort in Monday's win over the Mariners earn him a rotation spot or raise his profile as a potential part in a Ken Williams' trade package? For now, Hudson's six strikeouts and one earned run allowed over 6 2/3 innings get him this start vs. Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Danks moved over .500 for his career, at 41-40, with 7 2/3 scoreless innings thrown Tuesday at Safeco Field. The southpaw gave up one infield hit in the second and didn't give up another hit, solid or otherwise, until Ichiro's single with two outs in the eighth.
away_pitcher_note: After ending a three-game set at home against the Sox with a scoreless eight-inning effort, Felix begins the Mariners' four-game rematch on the road. He ranks among the league leaders in innings pitched and ERA, but lack of run support has affected his win output.

home_pitcher_note: Floyd was locked in a duel with Seattle ace Felix Hernandez on Wednesday. Floyd worked seven and did not allow a Seattle runner to reach scoring position. He has a 1.16 ERA over his past nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Rowland-Smith's last three starts have not gone well. He's allowed 14 earned runs in 13 1/3 innings, raising his ERA from 5.74 to 6.27. Manager Don Wakamatsu said Hyphen will stay in the rotation because he's part of the clubs long-term plans.

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle had his first complete game of the season in his last start, limiting the A's to one run on four hits. The 31-year-old has notched eight consecutive quality starts and has a 2.20 ERA in that span.
away_pitcher_note: With Cliff Lee gone, Vargas is the new complement to Felix Hernandez. He's in the AL's top 10 for ERA and has a quality start in eight of his past 10 appearances. Unfortunately, he's gotten just nine runs of support in his past seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia has been a pleasant surprise as a dependable back-of-the-rotation starter this season. Last time out, however, was a forgettable outing for the righty. He'll try to rebound after surrendering five earned runs in 1 1/3 innings vs. the A's.
away_pitcher_note: Pauley -- brought into the rotation as a spot starter -- has shown enough to keep himself around. In three starts, he's held opponents to just five earned runs. The next task is getting deeper into games, as he hasn't gone farther than six innings yet.

home_pitcher_note: Harrell is making his Major League debut on Friday against the A's. He was thrust into the start because the White Sox traded Daniel Hudson. He figures to be up for this one start before ceding his spot to Edwin Jackson.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson threw a successful 40-pitch side session on Wednesday, enabling the A's to activate him from the disabled list on Friday. It will be Anderson's first start since June 3, when he went down for the second time with elbow tendinitis.

home_pitcher_note: Danks was masterful yet again in his last start. This time, he outdueled Mariners ace Felix Hernandez, going eight innings and giving up one run. He tried to lobby manager Ozzie Guillen to pitch the ninth, but to no avail.
away_pitcher_note: Braden finally got the monkey off his back on Sunday, as he allowed three runs over 6 1/3 innings to earn the win in a 6-4 victory over the White Sox. It was the first victory in 10 tries for Braden following his perfect game on May 9.
